description: This class focuses on a hands-on approach to a variety of fine and practical arts skills. While drawing is used as a fundamental skill, things like sewing, printmaking, jewelry making and clay are all part of the crafts movement. While this class serves as a foundation gateway class it is geared more towards the practical arts than the fine arts. If you like working with your hands, this is a good class for you. Much like foundations in art, this is a gateway class for all classes in the art department.
fulfills_text: (Please note this course satisfies the Art graduation requirement)

description: Studio Art Drawing is an intermediate course focusing on drawing and design skills. Students will be exposed to a range of media and techniques to enhance their skills. A strong emphasis is also placed on composition. Students who have completed Foundations in Art or who have a waiver based on a submitted portfolio of drawing may qualify for the class. All abilities are welcome and evaluation is based on student improvement over the course of the semester vs. innate talent. This is predominantly a “hands on” class and also explores art history through presentations and web journeys. Portfolio development is supported.
prerequisites: Foundations of Art (Traditional class)

description: An intermediate course focused on developing an understanding of paint and color. Students will explore color through a variety of materials and techniques. While predominantly a “hands on” course, students will increase their understanding of color theory, art history, and composition, and be asked to respond to art through reading and writing. A partial list of materials may include pastel, watercolor, acrylic paint, and mixed media. *This course is offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT.
prerequisites: Studio Art 1 (Drawing and Design)
notes: Dual enrollment (college credit) course per catalog; see DUAL ENROLLMENT, pp.15-18

description: Ceramics are used throughout the world in myriad cultures for both their function and their form. Through hands-on projects students will develop patience and discipline while working with clay. Ceramic projects take a long time to complete from wet clay through two firings to a finished piece. This course requires students to balance production of multiple projects with good studio practice. Clay is a messy medium and students are required to maintain studio cleanliness; they will be given chores to help do so. The first half of the course is structured around developing skills with different techniques used to manipulate clay (e.g. slab building, coiling, sculpting, coiling, etc). The second half of the course is structured around artistic problems or questions that require students to think about the design, function, and aesthetics that they will use to solve the problem(s) posed. There is a lab fee of $10.00, which students are expected to pay. This fee helps to partially cover material, firing, and maintenance costs. Finances are different for everyone and if you have concerns you may talk to the teacher or to counseling if you are more comfortable. We may decide to waive the fee.
prerequisites: Strongly recommend Foundations (Traditional class)

description: This course offers disciplined and motivated students the opportunity to continue to develop skills in different techniques working with clay through hands-on projects. Students will be presented with artistic questions which they will have to explore through the medium of clay. The second part of the course is designated for students to work independently to develop their own series of work with a written artist statement to accompany it. There is a lab fee of $10.00, which students are expected to pay. This fee helps to partially cover material, firing, and maintenance costs. Finances are different for everyone and if you have concerns you may talk to the teacher or to counseling if you are more comfortable. We may decide to waive the fee. *This course is offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT.
prerequisites: Ceramics 1 with a grade of 75 or above or with department head approval.
notes: Dual enrollment (college credit) course per catalog; see DUAL ENROLLMENT, pp.15-18

description: This advanced course is tailored for self-motivated and disciplined students eager to elevate their proficiency in clay artistry through diverse techniques and hands-on projects. Emphasizing autonomy and creative exploration, students will grapple with profound artistic inquiries, using clay as a dynamic medium for expression. In the latter part of the course, students are empowered to chart their own artistic trajectory, developing a personalized series of work alongside a comprehensive written artist statement. This innovative approach encourages students to shape their unique vision within the realm of clay art. *This course is offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT.
prerequisites: Ceramics 2 with a grade of 75 or above or with department head approval.
notes: Dual enrollment (college credit) course per catalog; see DUAL ENROLLMENT, pp.15-18

description: Sculpture an intermediate level art class, allows students who have completed Foundations in Art to continue to work on 3 dimensional design problems. The assignments and materials provide a greater challenge than Foundations in Art, and students are given more creative freedom within the assignment framework. In keeping with the departmental philosophy, Sculpture is a discipline based art program in which students learn design theory, art history relevant to their work, and are required to think critically about their work. Various sculptural processes such as casting, relief sculpture, subtractive and additive processes are undertaken and some materials include wood, plaster, clay, and wire. While predominantly a "hands on" course, students will be asked to respond to art through reading and writing. Students will be expected to pay a $10 lab fee at the beginning of the course.
prerequisites: Strongly recommend Foundations of Art (traditional class) or Art of Crafts

description: This course is designed to build on the 3-dimensional design skills learned in Sculpture I and to create at an advanced level. Students will utilize their prior knowledge of color and surface quality, the work of great sculptors past and present, and technical skills to work “in the round” and relief. Casting, multi- piece molds, additive and subtractive methods will be part of the Sculpture II curriculum. Students will have the opportunity to work in teams to create public art that enhances the community. In addition to the creation of sculpture, students are expected to articulate their knowledge and experience through writing and class discussions. *This course is offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT.
prerequisites: Fine and Practical Art course and Sculpture I with a grade of 75 or above or with department head approval.
notes: Dual enrollment (college credit) course per catalog; see DUAL ENROLLMENT, pp.15-18

description: This course is a fusion of fiber art, fabrics and fashion. This course is geared towards beginning students’ exposure to technical knowledge in sewing and supports the artist sewer in problem solving creative projects. Sewing machine mechanics, accessories, and maintenance are explained and explored. Students will be introduced to many different types of fabrics, pattern making, hand sewing techniques, notions and more. Class time is mainly hands-on project time. This course draws upon the creative side of students to tap into artistic sewing pieces which may use non-traditional materials or non-traditional sewing craft. A wide variety of fabric is available in the classroom in addition to upcycled clothing donations in support of the art department's efforts of reducing environmental impact. This class includes an introductory fashion drawing unit which assists in satisfying the art graduation requirement or a student’s desire to take additional sewing or drawing coursework.
fulfills_text: (Please note this course satisfies the Art graduation requirement)

description: Independence and freedom in project choice will build on your previous learning. This course is for the student who is interested in learning more sewing and fiber art techniques in addition to having more freedom and project choice. As in Sewing 1, class time is largely hands-on with exploration in quilting, applique, knitting, crewel needlepoint and so much more. A wide variety of fabric is available in the classroom in addition to the upcycled clothing donations in support of the art departments’ efforts of reducing environmental impact. Students will learn how to apply their knowledge gained in Sewing 1 as well as complete a unit on fashion design.
prerequisites: Sewing 1

description: Students will learn about creating living environments that meet specific design concepts and needs. Through design projects students will create hands-on projects that relate to interior design alongside the textbook curriculum. Projects will revolve around drafting, furniture arrangement, and how to execute a storyboard for visual presentation. Storyboards will be created both by hand and by digital apps such as Canva. Art concepts covered are the elements of design, principles of design, and the role of color. This class is for the student who likes to take a personal style vision and develop it into a workable living space. Must have basic knowledge of measuring in order to successfully complete required floor plan drawings. This class is a good prerequisite for sewing and general art classes.
fulfills_text: (Please note this course satisfies the Art graduation requirement)

description: A studio course designed to build on the artistic skills acquired in the intermediate classes. Advanced techniques, materials, and concepts are explored through teacher presented studies and student developed projects. Student expression and independence is encouraged with teacher guidance. Portfolio development, both digitally and through collected work, can be used to facilitate entrance to art schools and related university studies. Techniques include drawing, printmaking, painting, 2D and 3D design, and non-traditional materials. Selected readings in art history and contemporary art will facilitate discussions and written responses. This course may be repeated for credit. *This course may also be offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT.
prerequisites: Studio Art I and II
notes: Catalog notes this course may also be offered for college credit (see DUAL ENROLLMENT)

description: AP Art will be a full year class and will replace the Advanced Art in the Community class as the Capstone for Visual and Performing Arts students. It will also be open to other juniors and seniors who have taken an advanced level of art. The class will heavily focus on portfolio development and strategies to be a successful working artist. The AP class will focus on sustained investigation, experimentation and communication of ideas in 2D and 3D art. It will focus on the development of skills, processes and concepts.
prerequisites: Grade of B or higher in an advanced level of a fine & practical art courses and recommendation from a F&PA teacher High proficiency in reading & writing and the use of technology, including Google Apps for Ed Strong desire to pursue a career or post-secondary education in the arts and develop community connections The ability to work independently and a strong drive to nurture one’s talents in the arts outside of school Transportation to and from studio visits or internship
notes: Prerequisite(s) listed as "See below"; the bullet list on p.55 is given in prerequisites

description: ● Students will learn the basic skills of graphic design (or digital art making) using industry standard, Mac based software. ● Students will produce digital and printed media using the following programs: Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator and Adobe InDesign. ● Students will learn to use the scanning equipment, digital camera file uploading, transferring and downloading files legally, making pdf files and other useful skills related to graphic arts.
prerequisites: None (prior experience and knowledge in the arts recommended)
fulfills_text: (Please note, this course satisfies the Art graduation requirement)

description: ● Students will take the basic skills learned in Computer Graphic Design I and apply them to producing more advanced graphic design artwork. ● Students will develop lifelong skills and prepare for post-secondary studies through creative projects and portfolio development. ● Students will have the opportunity to work independently and explore other media such as Weebly, Wix and After Effects. ● Students will connect with the school and local community to produce digital artwork for community events and programs (ie. logos, posters, web design, banners, newsletters, etc.). ● Students taking this course need to possess the ability to work independently and in groups, to be self-motivated, to be able to take constructive artistic criticisms and to be fluent in the Adobe software programs learned in Graphic Design I. ● This course may also be offered for optional college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT.
prerequisites: A grade of 75 or above in Computer Graphic Design I or permission of the instructor.
notes: Catalog notes this course may also be offered for college credit (see DUAL ENROLLMENT)

description: This course is designed for the interested photography student. Photo I covers all aspects of digital photography within an artistic context. Students will also be introduced to Digital Cameras, Adobe Lightroom, & Photoshop. 35mm photography is accessible for Photo I. Students will learn digital processing, how to print digitally processed photos. Students are expected to work independently, shooting photos after school, at home and during class (when specified). Course work includes shooting assignments, photo history, weekly journals, and a research paper/presentation on a personally selected photographer and the art of photography. Some cameras are available on loan for student use, but it is strongly recommended that you supply your own digital camera if possible.
fulfills_text: Digital Art Requirement

description: This course is designed for the motivated photography student. This is a continuation of the Photography 1 course. It covers all aspects of digital photography while introducing more advanced camera, lighting, and editing techniques. Students will have the opportunity to explore different photographic subjects and printing processes. Studio lighting will be introduced and used to gain a technical understanding of light and camera functions. Emphasis will be placed on independently developed challenges for each project, weekly journals, and monthly “revisits” of missed photographic opportunities. A cohesive portfolio of finished work will be expected of each student at the end of the term, including a digital portfolio. Some cameras are available on loan for student use, it is strongly recommended that the student supply their own digital camera if possible. *This course might also be offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT
prerequisites: Photography 1 with a grade of 75 or above or with department head approval.
notes: Catalog notes this course may also be offered for college credit (see DUAL ENROLLMENT)

description: This course is designed for the passionate photography student. This student will be self-guided but will work in the structure of the Photography 2 class with much higher expectations in the quality of produced work and more advanced challenges will be given to Photo 3 students with each assignment. A weekly journal is required along with review of missed photographic opportunities. Emphasis will be placed on student developed independent work. An extensive portfolio of work is required for the culmination of the course. Some cameras are available on loan for student use, but it is strongly recommended that the student supply their own digital camera if possible. *This course might also be offered for college credit; see DUAL ENROLLMENT
prerequisites: Photography II with a grade of 75 or above or with department head approval.
notes: Catalog notes this course may also be offered for college credit (see DUAL ENROLLMENT)

description: An independent project in art requires the student to have a strong sense of purpose and personal responsibility. This is not intended to duplicate existing courses. Content should be determined by the student in close consultation with the instructor prior to submitting the application to Mrs. Parker. The Art faculty is limited to no more than 3 independent students at any time, so Independent Studies will be competitive and limited.
prerequisites: Approval of instructor and Department Head
notes: Open to: Students who have completed all the courses in a particular field of study.

description: Food Fundamentals will teach you how to be comfortable in the kitchen through hands-on cooperative learning. You will learn about food preparation techniques, proper equipment usage, meal planning, purchasing techniques, nutrition, consumer issues, regional food and foreign food. You will explore the nutrient value in food, how appetite appeal affects what you eat, the social significance of how food plays into our choices, and cultural aspects of food. Students will have opportunities to have community guests in the classroom.
notes: Sub-heading: Family Consumer Sciences (credits satisfy elective requirements)

description: Using the skills learned in Foods Fundamentals students will further develop their skills with more advanced learning, community connections and hands-on food labs. This advanced study is based on nutrition, new food investigation, advanced cooking techniques, and the understanding of where food comes from along with recipe development. Curriculum is based on students interest and skill level.
prerequisites: Food Fundamentals
notes: Sub-heading: Family Consumer Sciences (credits satisfy elective requirements)

description: This class is designed to teach students how professional recordings are made and will give them the knowledge and tools to begin recording themselves at a high level. We will dive into how to use a DAW (digital audio workstation) to record, mix and master music. We will also learn about the different types of microphones, microphone placement, and other recording techniques that lead to high quality recordings. In addition to recording sound in a DAW, we will use midi controllers to create our own music in the class. By the end of this class, students will have an understanding of how to create a high quality recording of singers and instrumentalists. From the initial recording, to production after the fact. They will also learn how to create their own music using a DAW.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester / Fall 2026 / Spring 2027

description: Students who take this class will learn the basics of rock band instruments such as drums, bass, guitar and keyboard. They will learn from the teacher, peer mentors, and by self-teaching. As students advance their playing skills, they will have the chance to collaborate with one another in listening to songs they like and figuring out how to play the songs themselves. In addition to playing instruments, the class will listen to music from different eras and discuss the history and meaning behind the songs. Students will also have the chance to dabble in using Soundtrap to produce music electronically. Students will have homework and projects as part of this class.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Students will learn about and practice different skills that help them to write complete songs. This will include learning about song form/sections, melody, harmony, and rhythm. Students will study parts of language, learning how to use synonyms, adjectives, adverbs, imagery, and syllable count to write great lyrics. They will also work on their singing and learn how to play the guitar and learn what kinds of chord progressions support everyday songwriting. Students will work individually as well as in groups to sing, play, record, and give feedback to one another as they complete a variety of songwriting assignments.
prerequisites: Willingness and ability to sing alone during class.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Chorus is a full-year, four-credit class. All chorus members are required to attend all concerts in which the ensemble is performing, including evening concerts in November, March and May. Chorus students are taught about healthy and functional vocal technique, learn music literacy skills, and experience a wide variety of musical styles. Students are placed into sections (soprano, alto, tenor, and bass) and learn to sing advanced harmonies in 4- and 8-parts. Emphasis is placed on diction, dynamics, breath support, register use, expression, and interpretation. The chorus sings songs in many genres, meters, tempos, languages, arrangements and moods. While students learn to sing in a group, they are asked to reflect on their own musical identity and growth through class discussions and assignments. Students enrolling should be prepared to make this year-long commitment to the ensemble they are joining. If a student needs to enroll in Chorus for a single semester for two credits due to a schedule conflict, permission must be granted by the teacher prior to the beginning of the school year. This single semester option does not apply to students in grade nine.
prerequisites: Willingness and ability to participate fully by singing throughout all rehearsals and concerts. Previous chorus experience is highly recommended but not required.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Piano and Voice Studio is designed for students who are already BUHS Chorus. This class will meet every other day, opposite of Chorus. We will be learning proper vocal technique and expanding our keyboard skills. We will practice singing and playing our own parts in ensemble music, prepare for auditions, and practice solo works. We will learn how to effectively pick a solo work for your voice level, and how to develop it with guidance of the teacher. While this class is not an ensemble class, you will need to be ready to sing/play every day.
prerequisites: Students must be enrolled in Chorus or Honors Chorus
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester / Fall 2026 / Spring 2027

description: Visual and Performing Arts Academy Vocal Music strand students must enroll in this class for their junior and senior years. This course is open to chorus members, by audition, who want a more rigorous curriculum. Honors Chorus students rehearse and perform in the BUHS Chorus and must complete all the same requirements as other chorus members. In addition, they must: ● Audition for music festival choruses. ● Learn and perform a classical vocal solo at an annual vocal recital. ● Write a paper about their musical experiences throughout the year.
prerequisites: One+ year of high school chorus AND audition with the teacher. Students must be able to match pitch consistently when singing alone.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Our BUHS A Cappella Ensemble (Madrigals) is a vocal performance group and class. It is designed to offer vocal repertoire and class assignments that challenge students who are already familiar with vocal/choral technique and can sing in a small group setting. Vocalists auditioning for this ensemble must already be enrolled in chorus. This group meets one night per week with required attendance at all rehearsals and performances throughout the school year. Students are expected to practice their parts on their own each week at home. They will be given practice assignments (vocal practice tracks will be provided), and will periodically need to turn in recordings of themselves singing their songs for grades and credit. Students perform at regularly scheduled school concerts as well as community events around Brattleboro.
prerequisites: By audition only. Students must be enrolled in Chorus.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Full Year / Wednesdays, 6-8pm

description: Band is a full year, four credit class. Band students in all grade levels rehearse and perform together in one band. This performance course is designed to foster an understanding and love of music and music making as well as developing instrumental skills, artistic expression, and creativity. In large and small ensemble settings, band students will explore various musical styles and genres with a focus on standard and contemporary concert band literature as well as arrangements of Broadway and film scores, pop, and rock music. Instrument lessons scheduled during the school day are required for all band members and enable instruction to be differentiated for various instruments and ability levels. Individual achievement is monitored and guided through the use of performance assessments, both in the form of recorded playing tests and live solo performances. A regular routine of home practice is required as is attendance at all group performances, most of which happen outside of the school day. Students enrolling should be prepared to make this full year commitment to the ensemble. If a student needs to enroll in band for a single semester for two credits, permission must be granted by the teacher prior to the beginning of the school year. Students enrolled for a single semester must demonstrate proficiency in all of the performance indicators to earn course credit.
prerequisites: Recommendation from middle school band director and permission from high school band instructor
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Band Lab & Solo Works is designed for students who are already in BUHS Concert Band. This class will meet every other day, opposite of Band. We will be learning proper practice techniques. We will practice audition music, concert band music and solo works. We will focus on how to effectively pick a solo work for your instrument level, and how to develop it with the guidance of the teacher. While this class is not an ensemble class, you will need to be ready to play every day. Students will have a weekly 1:1 check-in with the teacher and weekly practice requirements.
prerequisites: Students must already be enrolled in Band or Honors Band
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester / Fall 2026 / Spring 2027

description: Visual and Performing Arts Academy Instrumental Music strand students must enroll in this class for their junior and senior years. The course is open to band members who want a more rigorous experience in Band. Students enrolled in the Honors Band rehearse and perform in the BUHS Band and complete all Band requirements. Additionally, students in the Honors Band are required to keep a practice log and share with the teacher weekly. They will perform in solo or small ensemble recitals in the winter and spring, and are expected to audition for one VMEA district festival, and the VMEA All State Festival, and are encouraged to play in the New England Music Festival Solo Festival. Honors Band students are required to complete a “music in the community” project, which may be playing in community groups, mentoring a younger student, performing with elementary students, performing for residents in nursing homes, or coaching a peer.
prerequisites: One+ years of high school band AND permission from instructor
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Full Year / Purple Days / Second Block

description: Jazz Ensemble is a performance course focusing on the study of various jazz styles in a big band setting. The curriculum combines an applied study of repertoire with introductory jazz theory and improvisation. Enrollment is strictly by audition and is limited to the standard jazz big band instrumentation of 2 alto saxes, 2 tenor saxes, 1 baritone sax, 4-5 trumpets, 4 trombones, piano, guitar, bass, and drums. Wind players and drummers must also be enrolled in Band. Music reading skills are required for all members. Jazz improvisation is a component of the class, although not the focus of the class. The class meets one night a week for two hours. The ensemble performs at all band concerts with occasional additional performances. Attendance at all evening rehearsals and performances is mandatory. Jazz Band is a full year, two-credit class. Students enrolling in the class should be prepared to make this year-long commitment to the ensemble they are joining and students are expected to practice their individual music parts on their own each week at home.
prerequisites: Audition and permission of instructor
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Full Year/ Evening / 2026-27

description: V.P.A. music students must take either this course or the V.P.A. Music Capstone: Senior Recital. They may also take both. This course requires students planning to audition for music schools to: ● Research schools ● Investigate audition requirements for schools they are applying to ● Receive guidance on the preparation of these materials from private instructors in the community ● Practice the solos and scales they will have to perform in the auditions. ● Record all information and submit it.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
notes: Open to: V.P.A. music students only

description: V.P.A. music students must take either this course or the V.P.A. Music Capstone: Audition Preparation. They may also take both. This course offers students the opportunity to prepare and perform a recital in the Spring. The course will take them through the process of: ● Working with a teacher of their instrument or voice in the to select and prepare repertoire for the recital ● Preparing for the recital in a focused, deliberate way ● Preparing a printed program including program notes ● Arranging for a performance venue and piano ● Contacting and rehearsing with an accompanist ● Advertising the recital and writing a press release ● Arranging all logistics for the recital ● Reflecting on the experience
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.
notes: Open to: Senior V.P.A. music students only

description: Fundamentals of Music is a course dedicated to teaching the basic concepts that all musicians should know. This class is designed for all students, whether or not you are already involved in the music department at BUHS. Students will learn skills and concepts such as how to read notes, read rhythm and navigate a piece of music. We will also spend time learning basic music theory such as how to read a key signature, time signature, and how to build a scale. Listening to music is also a large part of this class. We will learn active listening skills and use them as we listen to music from different time periods in our history. Additionally, we will spend time learning instruments, particularly piano.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: *Ability to read and play notes as written on a staff. This course is for vocal and instrumental students who are interested in playing jazz. Students will play jazz standards, learning how to interpret and enhance a melody, read chord symbols, drill scale and patterns, and ultimately improvise through a tune. We will also do a lot of listening to the recordings of jazz masters and contemporary musicians, discussing and emulating their singing and playing. We will learn some jazz history in order to understand the origins of this great music and pay our respects to it. Finally, we will learn how to prepare for a jam session or gig, as well as how to work with a band. The class will visit the Vermont Jazz Center to take advantage of their resources and events.
prerequisites: Recommendation from your band or chorus teacher, OR interview with instructor.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Students in this class will take a virtual trip around the world to find out what music is like around the globe! From salsa music to Mongolian Metal to yodeling and K-pop, we explore the characteristics of music from different countries and cultures. In this class, we will learn about the instruments, rhythms, songs and dances associated with world music. We will explore what music from different parts of the world has in common and what makes it distinct. Students in this class should be prepared to listen to music and watch videos, participate in class discussions, and play percussion instruments (no previous experience required).
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: This course is designed to explore the history of Rock ‘n Roll by analyzing, studying and performing its songs. We will be learning about cultural influences on Rock, listening to music representing different stages in its development, and performing songs by major artists. Students will be advancing individual guitar skills for both rhythm and lead guitar as well as discovering the basics of harmony used in Rock ‘n Roll. Guitars will be supplied for students.
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Visual and Performing Arts Academy students in a music strand must take this class. This course is designed to give students a deep understanding of three fundamental aspects of music theory: rhythm, melody and harmony. A variety of composition projects are designed to follow instruction in these three areas, allowing students to create meaning of the information and apply it in authentic ways. Noteflight music notation program enables students to compose, edit and share their work. Inside Music web-based composition instructional units are used extensively. This rigorous class is best suited for students with some background in music. It is highly recommended for students planning to further pursue music after high school. Topics uncovered include meter, rhythm, time signatures, clefs, pitch notation, major and minor scales, melodic analysis, connections of text to music, motive, form, chords (diatonic and non-diatonic), connection of melody to harmony, chord progressions and analysis.
prerequisites: Basic music background and interview with instructor
fulfills_text: A graduation credit in the arts can be earned in music classes.

description: Skill development, and participation in a wide variety of activities including individual and team sports, physical fitness programs, leadership development and lifetime activities.
prerequisites: None (Recommended for 9th grade students)

description: Lifetime and Leisure Activities consist of activities that students can do on their own and can continue to do throughout their lives, either individually or with a partner/small group. These activities can also include personal fitness. Students will demonstrate the ability to exhibit responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others in physical activity settings; and demonstrate the ability to value physical activity for health, enjoyment, challenge, self-expression, and/or social interaction. This course will build upon previously learned skills and activities developed in Foundations of Physical Education.
prerequisites: PE 1
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester/alternating days (can take this twice with department head permission)

description: Develop the ability to achieve and maintain a health enhancing level of physical fitness. Students will learn the theory and skill development of different health-related fitness components;Physiological benefits of training; and the effects of training on the body. Students will learn how to design and/or incorporate their own workout programs or that support a physically active and healthy lifestyle.
prerequisites: PE 1
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester/alternating days (Can take this twice with department head permission)

description: Students will demonstrate competency in motor skills and movement patterns needed to successfully participate in selected competitive sports; demonstrate the ability to use movement concepts, principles, strategies, and tactics as they apply to the learning and performance of team, dual and individual sport activities; and demonstrate the ability to participate regularly in physical activity. This course will build upon previously learned skills and activities developed in Foundations of Physical Education.
prerequisites: PE 1
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester/block/alternating days (Can take this twice with department head permission)

description: This is not an option for students to complete during their ninth grade or senior years. A physical education equivalent can be satisfied by successfully participating in and completing two (2) different JV or Varsity sports during the same school year. Course credit is given to students who earn a certificate of participation as determined by the team coach. This is a pass/fail course with no effect on GPA. Furthermore, it does not count as a class to be used in determining full-time student status.
prerequisites: Successful completion of PE 1. Students must have already earned 2 PE credits before choosing this option.
fulfills_text: A physical education equivalent can be satisfied by successfully participating in and completing two (2) different JV or Varsity sports during the same school year.

prerequisites: Per case manager
offering_note: Schedule as printed: Semester / Alternating days

description: This course provides students with instruction in Health Education according to the Vermont Comprehensive Health Education Program. It is designed to meet the needs of students in accordance with their stages of physical, mental, and social development as well as promote healthy choices. Health Education addresses current issues through units on nutrition & physical activity; bullying & violence prevention; suicide prevention; alcohol, tobacco & other drugs; human sexuality; and healthy relationships. An emphasis is placed on activities designed to build self-efficacy around health skills including decision making skills, goal setting, communication skills, and health advocacy.
fulfills_text: required for graduation
notes: Open to: Grades 10-12 (required for graduation)

description: Recommended: Mentoring & Leadership This course builds upon concepts learned in Health (9th/10th grade). Students in Teaching Health in Elementary Schools will explore concepts of mentoring and teaching, and complete a practical application at local elementary schools in order to promote Health Standards of the Vermont Comprehensive Health Education Program. Students will choose a health focus area (nutrition, injury prevention, drugs/medicine, infectious disease, mental/emotional health and relationship health) and develop age appropriate activities & curriculum to implement with elementary students. Activities will also emphasize skills including decision making skills, goal setting, and communication skills. Grading for this course will be based on the successful planning of several health lessons for elementary grades AND visiting those classrooms and teaching the lessons. Students in this course must exhibit a very high level of responsibility, as they will be expected to travel outside of BUHS during regular school hours. Transportation will be required, or parent permission to travel with someone else in a personal vehicle.
prerequisites: Health

course_name: CPR, First Aid & Wilderness First Aid
description: In this hands-on, practical course, students will learn critical life-saving skills that can be applied in everyday situations and emergency scenarios. The curriculum covers three main areas: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) & AED, basic First Aid, and Wilderness First Aid. Students will gain proficiency in recognizing medical emergencies, using an AED, performing CPR, and providing first aid for common injuries and illnesses. After covering basic first aid techniques, additional emphasis will be placed on first aid techniques in outdoor and remote environments, where professional medical help may be delayed. Key topics include wound care, splinting, hypothermia, heat-related illnesses, snake bites, and other wilderness-specific emergencies. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to respond confidently in both urban and wilderness settings, with the ability to stabilize injured individuals until professional medical help arrives. The course includes certification in CPR and First Aid, ensuring students are well-equipped to handle a wide range of emergency situations. Key Skills Covered: ● Using an AED when one is available ● Performing CPR on adults, children, and infants ● Recognizing and treating common medical emergencies ● Administering first aid for cuts, burns, fractures, and sprains ● Wilderness-specific first aid techniques (e.g., treating hypothermia, insect bites, and dehydration) ● Responding to environmental hazards like extreme heat or cold Grading in this class will be a reflection of active demonstration of learned skills, scores on content-based quizzes, and performance-based role playing of medical emergencies. Active participation will be required.
prerequisites: Health

description: The Vermont Agency of Education (AOE) has established a number of programs through which Vermont high school students can earn both high school and college credit for certain courses they take while in high school. ● “Concurrent” Dual Enrollment (DE) courses are courses taught at BUHS by BUHS faculty who are also adjunct professors with the partner college. Students will gain and demonstrate transferable skills that are essential for career readiness and global citizenship in the 21st century. These competencies include: proficiency in a second language; social and intercultural awareness and skills; an understanding of the connections among political, geographical, historical, cultural, religious, and economic systems. Students who successfully complete ISA requirements will receive a designation on their transcripts.
notes: program. Current 8th, 9th, and 10th grade students may apply; requirements listed on pp.22-23

description: AP Computer Science A is a rigorous, college-level programming course that expands on the foundational skills learned in Computer Science 2 or 3. Students will develop proficiency in object-oriented programming using programming language Java while learning to design, implement, test, and refine software solutions to real-world problems. Key topics include creating and using classes and objects, working with complex data structures such as arrays and ArrayLists, developing algorithms that store and process data, and evaluating the efficiency and correctness of different solutions. Students will also examine broader impacts of computing, including responsible use, ethical considerations, and the social implications of software systems. The course concludes with the AP Computer Science A Exam. AP CSA is offered every other year and will run during the 2026–2027 school year.
prerequisites: Teacher recommendation andearn a 80% or higher in Computer Science 2 or Computer Science 3
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Curiosity & Creativity

description: Computer science touches every part of modern life, and learning to think like a computer scientist – designing solutions, writing programs, tackling challenges – gives you the power to create almost anything you can imagine. Really, it’s like a super power! This course is as much about programming and learning core computer science concepts as it is about creativity, design and problem-solving. We’ll work in Scratch, a block-based programing language ideal for complete beginners as well as those with some programming experience who want a space to explore creative computing. Most assignments project-based, with freedom to design and develop your own original programs. Students earning an 80% or higher are eligible to continue on to Computer Science 2: Programming with Python
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Curiosity & Creativity

description: Physical computing forms the basis of smart devices, wearables like smart watches, e-textiles and IoT (Internet of Things) devices. In this semester course, you will learn to design electronic devices that interact with the physical world by building circuits and writing programs that run on microcontrollers (tiny, hand-held computers). You might build a robot arm that can draw, a racetrack that times the speed of a toy car, a small greenhouse that opens a vent if the temperature gets too hot – what you build is up to you! This course is project based and highly self-directed; you will have lots of freedom to pursue your own projects. We will utilize the Arduino microcontroller in projects and the programming language C++.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Computer Science II with at least an 80% or AP Computer Science A with at least a 70%; or demonstrate prior programming experience to the teacher to determine course placement
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Curiosity & Creativity

description: In this course, we will learn how to design and build web pages using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and site builders. We’ll examine how thoughtful design choices improve user experience - from making sites more accessible and easier to navigate, to applying principles of visual design to create polished, visually appealing pages. During the first half of the course, we’ll focus on best practices for working with markup languages and learn how to make sites interactive with JavaScript. We’ll also explore how AI tools can support the development of more advanced features. In the second half, our attention will shift toward site builders and design. This is a project-based course with plenty of opportunities to create your own original websites. Students earning an 80% or higher are eligible to continue on to Computer Science 2: Programming with Python.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Curiosity & Creativity

Class will involve note taking, research, quizzes and tests, but will focus heavily on hands-on projects. description: The 9th grade English program focuses on three core questions: Who am I? What is my community? How do I fit into the world? We practice three English reading and writing skills: annotation, speaking and listening, and evidence-based writing. This class will be co-assigned and team-taught with Humanities Civics and World Societies. Texts may include: Long Way Down by Jason Reynolds, Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare, Braiding Sweetgrass by Robin Wall Kimmerer, Night by Elie Wiesel, To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee, and Of Mice and Men by John Steinbeck. Earned Honors: Students have the option to earn Honors credit in this class by demonstrating learning throughout the school year at an Honors level. The earned Honors designation will be awarded at the end of year and enables students to take English 10 Honors (Genre) in 10th grade.

description: Can literature capture what it means to be an American? How does it inform our understanding of racial, class, and gender divides? These are some of the questions we will be asking as we engage with a variety of texts spanning the previous century. We will look at poetry, short stories, and novels from the era, placing them in their larger historical and cultural contexts. Close reading and writing will be emphasized throughout the semester. We will study literature with the assumption that art both shapes and reflects culture. Some writers we may read include F. Scott Fitzgerals, Jack Kerouac, and Toni Morrison.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving, Curiosity and Creativity, Effective Communication.

description: This course offers an introduction to African American literature. Students will read and engage with poetry, short stories, essays, and novels written by African American writers from varied time periods and literary movements as they look for how these texts relate, converse, revise, or depend upon each other. Students will evaluate essays, poems, and novels written by writers such as Zora Neale Hurston, Maya Angelou, James Baldwin, Ta-Nehisi Coates, Toni Morrison and Octavia Butler. We will respond to the works we study with academic essays and creative projects.
prerequisites: Successful completion of 10th grade English.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Cross-Cultural Understanding & Civic Engagement.

description: Students explore the darker aspects of human nature through 19th century American stories about the influence of evil, self righteousness, and psychological angst. These worlds are often haunted by female heroines, supernatural elements, and the fears born out of the beginnings of a new nation.
prerequisites: Successful completion of 10th grade English.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Cross-Cultural Understanding & Civic Engagement.

description: The AP English Language and Composition course focuses on the development and revision of evidence-based analytic and argumentative writing, the rhetorical analysis of nonfiction texts, and the decisions writers make as they compose and revise. Students evaluate, synthesize, and cite research to support their arguments. Additionally, they read and analyze rhetorical elements and their effects in nonfiction-- including images as forms of texts-- from a range of disciplines and historical periods.This course provides preparation for the AP examination in AP English Language and Composition.
prerequisites: Teacher Recommendation. Completion of a summer assignment is required for enrollment in this course.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development; Effective Communication. | *BHS partners with Saint Michael’s College to offer this course as a concurrent enrollment class. description: This year-long course is designed for students who want to expand their awareness of language, strengthen their critical reading of poetry and fiction, and further develop their writing style. To understand the power of the written word students will be reading and evaluating the works of established writers, while also writing and evaluating their own writing using the writing process of drafting, editing and revising. Students will be active readers as well as writers, engaging in thoughtful discussions about the role of the writer and the individual in an ever-changing world. This course is concerned with the individual's search for identity, embracing not just the issue of freedom, but also the problems of responsibility and commitment. Novels, short stories, poems and essays are used to examine the themes of fate and free will, illusion and reality, the nature of justice and the question of identity. While examining such themes, students will read critically to determine an author’s purpose, audience, literary strategies, and style and provide evidence of their understanding through class discussions and writings. Students should expect to read and write extensively in this course. This course provides preparation for the AP examination in English Literature and Composition. Major works to be studied may include but are not limited to: Man's Search for Meaning, Blood Dazzler, Slaughterhouse Five, Crime and Punishment, Frankenstein, One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, The Stranger, Waiting for Godot, Beloved, and Invisible Man. Students taking this course are able to demonstrate the ability to do college level work by analyzing literature in depth and writing multiple essays of analysis. Completion of a summer assignment is required for enrollment in this course.
