description: What makes a great movie? Cinema Studies provides the tools to understand and analyze films. We’ll learn about the ways that directors decide on the camera work, set and costume design, and editing to bring their visions to the screen. We will watch films by a variety of directors, each with their own style and approach to storytelling. We will look at how movies have evolved over time. We will analyze camera angles, lighting, sound, and read and write movie reviews. Projects may include storyboarding films, staging photographs to replicate common camera angles and techniques, studying and reviewing a film or a series of films independently, and completing an analysis of a movie’s techniques and values.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Effective Communication

description: This course provides students with opportunities to improve and expand their writing skills. Students will develop an awareness of language, read with more critical understanding, and develop an individual writing style. Writing is a process, which involves prewriting, drafting, revising, and editing. Correct grammar and effective language are a focus of the course. Students read and analyze essays of narration, description, process analysis, comparison and contrast, division and classification, definition, cause and effect, and persuasion and argument. Then, they write their own essays in these styles. This class becomes a writing community where students share and discuss ideas, thoughts, and works. The main focus of this class is writing, but we will also address standards and benchmarks of reading and writing, with an emphasis on writing clear, concise papers that reflect the proper use of the conventions of English.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication; Curiosity and Creativity; Personal Development.

description: Contemporary literature is often defined as “post-war” (WWII). In this class, students will explore contemporary literature by examining the human experience through texts that belong to and speak to the present. Students drive the lines of inquiry and will read poetry, short stories, and novels, and watch films to gain a deeper understanding of the human condition today. Course proficiencies focus on critical thinking, close reading, and creativity. Students will keep a journal, share their writing and thinking, and formally present their understanding. Units of study may include: post-apocalyptic literature, postmodern storytelling techniques, and a choice-read unit. Core texts may include but are not limited to The Road and Memento.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving, Curiosity and Creativity, Effective Communication.

description: How do we effectively craft and tell stories? This semester long course is aimed at developing creative writing skills through composition, critique, and revision in an intensive workshop format. Students will explore writing as a process while also sharpening the ability to evaluate creative writings. Students will create short stories, poems, plays, and more. As a class, we will work toward understanding the purposes and motives behind writing. The elements and techniques that go into an effective piece will be constantly analyzed and discussed so that students will perceive some of the various formulas authors use to create immortal, effective art. Students will post and publish work online and in print to reach a wide variety of audiences.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication, Curiosity & Creativity.

description: This course examines books, speeches, movies, documentaries, and other forms of media centered around topics which have inspired fear in Americans. Through in-depth discussions, we will unpack the role that fear has played in shaping American culture, and attempt to understand the core fears upon which these topics are hinged. Students will practice analytical writing, creative writing and dialogue. Units of study may include War of the Worlds (radio broadcast), Poltergeist, The Bad Seed, Skeleton Crew, “The Lottery,” Psycho, Interview with a Vampire, Baby Teeth, Black Mirror,Twilight Zone, The Final Girl Support Group, The Blair Witch Project, and The Amityville Horror.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical thinking and problem solving, curiosity and creativity

description: This elective course is designed to give students an in-depth look at both the reading and writing of poetry. Students will examine works by established poets from various movements and cultures throughout the ages. Students will study poetic language, symbolism and themes, as well as voice, style and purpose. Students will engage in reading, reciting and analyzing poetry, as well as creating their own original, poetic works, which will be first edited by a conference partner and then shared with the class upon completion. Proficiency in these areas will be assessed throughout the course.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication; Curiosity and Creativity; Civic Engagement & Cross-Cultural Understanding.

description: This course will include reading, discussion, and written analysis of several major plays and some of the sonnets. The course explores Shakespeare’s challenging language and the memorable characters that populate his works, including kings, queens, lovers, shrews and fools. Themes such as power, revenge, love, jealousy, ambition and betrayal will be discussed. Critical approaches including psychological, feminist, and historical theories may be presented and applied to the texts.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Creativity and Curiosity, Personal Development

description: Speech class will help students to become more effective and confident public speakers. This class offers students the opportunity to learn the fundamentals of public speaking and to study the basics of communication theory. Students will develop individual speaking styles and study the intricacies of effective speech and improve their writing through a process that includes pre-writing, drafting, revising, and editing. Students will choose their own topics to write with purpose: to inform, to entertain, to argue, and to persuade. Students will also address standards of reading, as we study speeches from history and communication theory. This class values creating a writing community where students openly share and discuss ideas, thoughts, and works.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication; Personal Development.

description: In this course, you’ll explore how stories work and why they matter to us. We’ll read a wide range of fiction, from classic and contemporary writers like Alice Walker, Octavia Butler, and Samanta Schweblin. You’ll learn how characters develop, how authors build themes, and how point of view shapes meaning. You’ll practice close reading, collaborative annotation, and literary interpretation using different lenses such as feminist, psychological, or historical. Through discussions, writing, and media, you’ll strengthen your critical thinking and discover how stories connect to your own life and identity.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical thinking and problem solving; Effective Communication.

description: Students read and discuss literature about and by women who have investigated, challenged, and shaped notions of womanhood. This is a survey course. Students read challenging essays, plays, poems, short stories, articles, and novels. Students write extensively, and engage in seminar-style class discussions in this college-preparatory level class. Texts may include Passing by Nella Larsen, The Bluest Eye by Toni Morrison, Woman Warrior by Maxine Hong Kingston, and The Awakening by Kate Chopin.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical thinking and problem solving; Effective Communication

description: World Literature investigates global cultural perspectives about universal human ideas like forgiveness, family, truth, and what it really means “to live a good life.” We will read books and watch films from diverse world creators based on their culture, compare them to each other, and to our own cultural perspective. This is a writing and discussion-based course that will focus on analysis and comparison of ideas, asking you to become cultural investigators and appreciators of perspectives very different from your own.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Cross-Cultural Understanding & Civic Engagement Department of Multilingual Learners

description: This course provides basic language instruction to new English language speakers in all four domains. This class is designed for EL students who have very limited English proficiency.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 1-2.

description: This initial reading course provides newcomer students instruction in the foundations of literacy in English. Students will learn the English phonetic systems, early literacy skills, and language needed to continue reading courses at Burlington High School. Students will develop basic reading and comprehension skills.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 1-2.

description: This course develops background knowledge of natural processes and basic scientific concepts, principles, theory, methods, and essential vocabulary. A hands-on approach will be used to establish comprehension.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 1-2 .

description: The goal of this course is to develop background knowledge of world geography and cultures. Students will focus on developing a comprehension of and use of concepts and skills necessary for reading primary sources and non-fiction texts, writing evidence based paragraphs, creating presentations of learning, and participating in research activities in social studies. Social studies concepts will be introduced such as concepts of historical past, timelines and chronology, geographical terms, map usage terms, economic terms, role of culture and concepts of tradition. The proficiencies introduced in this course mirrors the ninth grade social studies proficiencies to facilitate students moving into the mainstream after achieving a foundation of English language and social studies skills.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 2.

description: The goal of this course is to provide basic direct reading instruction to beginning English language learners. This course is designed to assist students in developing English language reading skills. Upon successful completion of Reading 1, and depending on English and language skill proficiency, students will take Supplemental Reading, Lexia, or Reading 2 classes.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 1-2 and/or Lexile level BR0-L100.

description: Year 1 and 2. This is a skills-based class that will focus on strengthening the foundations of reading: decoding, fluency, reading comprehension, and vocabulary. This course will include opportunities for whole class discussions and collaboration, small group work, and independent practice. Everyone can become a better, more successful reader and the goal for this course is to provide the skills and strategies that students can apply across settings to improve their reading and understanding of text. This course will run for a half block each day.
prerequisites: ML Department Recommendation, IXL 0-200, review of SRI Scores and testing data
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication

description: The goal of this course is to provide language instruction to English language learners in order to continue to develop students’ English language proficiency in all four language domains of reading, writing, speaking and listening in English.
prerequisites: ELP Level 2.

description: Students in this course develop background knowledge of U.S. History and Government. Students will focus on developing a comprehension of and use of concepts and skills necessary for reading non-fiction texts and primary sources, writing evidence based paragraphs and participating in research activities in mainstream social studies courses. Students will learn terms related to historical past, timelines and chronology, geography, map usage, economy, government, culture, and concepts of tradition, heritage, history, immigration and migration, freedom, and slavery. This course is designed to meet American History standards for those students who enter BHS having not had an American History class.
prerequisites: ELP Level 2.

description: This course provides reading instruction to English language learners to further develop their English language reading skills. Students will develop vocabulary and writing skills while reading increasingly complex texts.
prerequisites: ELP Level 2 and/or Lexile level BR0-300.

description: The goal of this course is to develop background knowledge of the natural processes as well as the basic scientific concepts, principles, theory, method and essential vocabulary to English learners who lack an educational background or the language necessary for mainstream science. Students in this class will continue to use a hands-on approach to establish comprehension.
prerequisites: ELP Level 2-3. INTERMEDIATE ENGLISH Levels 3-5

description: This course provides language instruction to English learners at an ELP proficiency level 3, in order to advance their development of English in all four language domains and to help students prepare for mainstream English classes. This course will build upon those skills learned in EL English 2.
prerequisites: ELP Writing Level 3.

description: This course provides reading instruction to English language learners to further develop their English language reading skills. Students will develop vocabulary, morphology and comprehension skills while reading increasingly complex texts.
prerequisites: ELP Level 3 and/or Lexile level 200-500.

description: The goal of this course is to provide language instruction to English language learners at a Proficiency Level 3.5 to 4, further advance ELs academic English skills in all four language domains, and help students transition to mainstream English classes. This course also focuses on the 9th and 10th grade English proficiencies of annotating, summarizing and speaking. This course will build upon those skills learned in English Language 3.
prerequisites: ELP Writing Level 4.

description: This class is a support class for English language learners concurrently enrolled in the co-taught 9th grade Humanities and Earth Science. This course will provide students with additional language instruction necessary to succeed in English 9/ Humanities and Earth Science, as well as continue to develop and refine English language skills in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. Placement will be based on reading assessments and will be based on ELL ACCESS scores.
prerequisites: Enrollment in 9th grade Humanities/Civics/Earth Science. ELP Level 3-5.

description: This class supports EL students also enrolled in World History and Biology or Chemistry in order to provide additional instruction, vocabulary and language development, and research assistance to ensure student academic success in mainstream history and science classes.
prerequisites: Enrollment in World History or Biology ELP Level 3.5-5, or other science elective.

description: This supported EL introduction to science course emphasizes laboratory skills and safety. Basic chemistry concepts including matter, compounds, chemical bonding, chemical equations and chemical reactions are included in this course.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 3-4.
notes: Also listed on p.92 of main catalog as 'Introduction to Chemistry' (Science & Technology); text differs from this entry; prerequisite there: Successful completion of Science 2 or equivalent and/or WIDA Level 2-3

description: This course develops background knowledge on the five units in Health Education: Mental Health, Nutrition, Substance Abuse, Relationships and Sexuality. There is a specific focus on concepts, principles, and essential vocabulary. This class is designed for EL students who have limited English proficiency.
prerequisites: ELP Levels 2-3

course_name: College & Career Readiness for Multilingual Learners
description: This course helps multilingual students prepare for life after high school by exploring college options, career pathways, and workplace expectations. Students build academic English while practicing real-world skills such as goal-setting, resume writing, interviewing, and navigating applications and financial aid. By the end of the course, students create a personalized plan for their post-secondary goals.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This course builds speaking and communication skills for English language learners. Students practice real-world and academic communication through discussions, presentations, and collaborative activities.
prerequisites: Teacher Recommendation

description: This introductory singing class is designed for students with little to no formal music ensemble or singing experience. This course is a space for EL students as well as students who have never seen sheet music or made music in a formal group setting before to learn the fundamentals of singing through a variety of songs and genres in a slow-paced, student-driven, and supportive group environment.

AP 2D Art and Design is a portfolio driven course where students create a collection of artwork and designs showing both technical skill and individual creative exploration. Using a variety of different media and techniques students will explore their ideas in a year long creative journey. Students will be exposed to advanced 2D Art and Design concepts and will keep a year-long sketchbook. Students must bring creative forces and imagination to their own education and development. These qualities are encouraged and stimulated through open ended assignments and refined through class interaction and critique. Students should be prepared to make and talk about art both on a philosophical and conceptual level. This course is ideal for students who are self-driven, want to challenge themselves, or are creating a portfolio for college applications. AP 2D Art and Design is a rigorous course and requires an exceptional work ethic.
prerequisites: 4 semesters of art courses AND portfolio / permission of instructor
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem

description: AP Drawing is a portfolio driven course where students create a collection of artwork and designs showing both technical drawing skill and individual creative exploration. Using a variety of different media and techniques students will explore their ideas in a year long creative journey. Students must bring creative forces and imagination to their own education and development. These qualities are encouraged and stimulated through open ended assignments and refined through class interaction and critique. Students should be prepared to make and talk about art both on a philosophical and conceptual level. This course is ideal for students who are self-driven, want to challenge themselves, or are creating a portfolio for college applications. AP Drawing is a rigorous course and requires an exceptional work ethic.
prerequisites: 4 semesters of art courses AND portfolio / permission of instructor
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: AP Art History is an introductory college-level art history course. Students cultivate their understanding of art history through analyzing works of art and placing them in historical context as they explore concepts like culture and cultural interactions, theories and interpretations of art, the impact of materials, processes, and techniques on art and art making, and understanding purpose and audience in art historical analysis.
prerequisites: 1 Credit of Visual Art
notes: Student cap: 20 | Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

course_name: Art Foundations (Formerly known as Art I)
description: This semester-long studio course is designed to provide students with the foundational knowledge and skills to practice the creative process of creating, presenting, responding, and connecting through the visual arts. Students will strengthen their discipline literacy of the elements of art as they explore a variety of media, techniques, and design concepts. This course will develop creative thinking and problem solving skills, observational skills, and build self-expression and reflection. Art Foundations is a prerequisite for all upper level art classes.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This is an introductory ceramics course focused primarily on building foundational skills in hand-building and supplemented by opportunities to explore basic wheel-throwing techniques. Students will learn pinch pot, coil and slab construction methods, as well as surface decoration, glazing processes and safe studio practices. Through guided practice and projects, students will gain an understanding of the properties of clay, the stages of the ceramic process, and the artistic possibilities of working in three dimensions.
prerequisites: Successful Completion of Art Foundations (formerly known as Art I)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity, Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

description: This is an intermediate course for students who wish to further develop their skills. Students will advance their hand-building abilities, strengthen wheel-throwing techniques, and explore a range of surface treatments and glazing methods. The course emphasizes refined craftsmanship, creative problem-solving, and the development of personal artistic style.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Ceramics I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity, Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

description: Drawing 1 is an introductory studio art course that teaches the essential skills of observational and creative drawing. Students explore line, value, proportion, shading, and perspective while working with a variety of mediums. Projects emphasize the elements of art and principles of design, encouraging both technical growth and personal expression. Students will also learn basic critique skills and study selected artists for inspiration. By the end of the course, each student will develop a small portfolio demonstrating improved technique and creativity.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Art Foundations (formerly known as Art I)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Drawing 2 is an intermediate, studio-based course designed to continue building students’ skills in drawing. Through hands-on practice, students will learn the essential techniques, concepts, and processes used in observational and imaginative drawing. Drawing 2 will be encouraged to find and practice their own style while applying the elements of art and principles of design to demonstrate their understanding of visual literacy. In addition to studio work, students will develop their ability to critique artwork, reflect on their creative choices, and discuss artistic techniques using appropriate vocabulary. By the end of the course, students will have a portfolio of finished drawings that demonstrate technical growth, creativity, and problem-solving.
prerequisites: Drawing I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This introductory studio course in Fiber Arts explores natural and synthetic fiber materials as the primary media to create sculptural artworks. Students will explore a variety of fibers and fiber techniques, focusing on elements of art, principles of design, historical context, and applying it to their own creative expression. Students will study fiber artists and their works, culminating in hands-on projects, critical analysis, and exhibition of their own artworks. Students will build technical skills and vocabulary to successfully pursue upper level fiber art courses.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Art Foundations (formerly known as Art I)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity, Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

description: In this intermediate-level course, students explore a selection of diverse concepts, materials, and processes associated with contemporary fiber arts. Emphasis will be on defining the line between craft and fine art, expanding conceptual development as well as furthering students' technical skills. The course will address the process and development of transforming ideas into form, and pushing the boundaries of traditional craft for visual storytelling.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Fiber Arts I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity, Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

course_name: Mixed Media I (Formerly known as Art II)
description: This is a studio course that introduces students to the combined use of drawing, painting, collage and digital media. Students will develop technical skills and creative problem-solving techniques as they explore how multiple materials and processes can be integrated into cohesive artworks. Coursework emphasizes composition, material experimentation, and thoughtful artistic decision-making. By the end of the course, students will complete a portfolio of original mixed-media pieces and gain a deeper understanding of how diverse media can be used to communicate ideas and personal expression.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Drawing I or Painting I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

course_name: Mixed Media II (Formerly known as Art II)
description: This course builds on foundational mixed media skills to help students develop a more personal and sophisticated artistic voice. Through layered exploration of drawing, painting, collage, printmaking, sculpture and digital processes, students learn to combine materials with intention and craftsmanship. Emphasis is placed on creative problem-solving, concept development, experimentation and refining technical skills.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Mixed Media I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Painting 1 is an introductory art course that teaches students the basic skills and techniques of painting. Students learn how to use different painting materials—such as acrylics and watercolors—and explore fundamental concepts like color theory, composition, and brushwork. The class includes guided projects that help students develop creativity, observation skills, and confidence in their artistic abilities.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Art Foundations (formerly known as Art I)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Painting 2 is an intermediate course designed for students who have completed Painting I and want to deepen their artistic skills. Students explore more advanced techniques in acrylic, watercolor, and mixed media while studying color harmony, style, and personal expression. Projects encourage creativity, problem-solving, and the development of a personal artistic voice. Emphasis is placed on refining technique, experimenting with new approaches, and building a strong portfolio.
prerequisites: Painting I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Printmaking is an introductory art course that teaches students how to create images using a variety of printmaking techniques. Students explore methods such as relief printing, monoprinting, and collagraphs while learning about design, craftsmanship, and safe studio practices. The course emphasizes creativity, experimentation, and developing strong visual ideas.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Art Foundations (formerly known as Art I)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Sculpture 1 is an introductory studio course in three-dimensional (3D) art making. Students will explore a variety of sculpture techniques with diverse media, including found materials, focusing on elements of art, principles of design, historical context, and applying it to their own creative expression. Students will study sculptors and their works, culminating in hands-on projects, critical analysis, and exhibition of their own artworks. Students will build skills and vocabulary to successfully pursue upper level sculpture courses.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Art Foundations (formerly known as Art I)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: In this intermediate-level course, students explore a selection of diverse concepts, materials, and processes associated with contemporary sculpture. Students will experience a variety of additive and subtractive sculpture techniques through various media. Emphasis will be on exploring alternative methods of art production, expanding conceptual development as well as furthering students' technical skills. The course will address the process and development of transforming ideas into form.
prerequisites: Sculpture I
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This introductory guitar class is designed for students with diverse abilities and little or no guitar experience. Utilizing guitars provided by the school and adaptive techniques, students will learn the fundamentals of playing, reading, and writing guitar music in an inclusive and supportive environment.
prerequisites: School-based team referral required.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This course is designed for students who are curious about how music really works, how melodies are built, how harmonies fit together, and what gives music its structure and meaning. AP Music Theory introduces the foundations of harmony and melody as the first year of a college-level music theory sequence. Students begin with essential skills such as note and rhythm reading, intervals, and scales, and then progress to harmonies, chord progressions, ear training, melodic analysis, and composition. By the end of the year, students are prepared to take the Advanced Placement exam, which may allow them to earn college credit, skip a year of college music theory, and/or receive fine arts credit—giving them a strong head start in their musical journey. Successful students typically enter the course with some musical background and basic note-reading skills in at least one clef. While it is strongly encouraged that students in BHS performing ensembles continue in those classes alongside AP Music Theory, since each course supports and strengthens the other, students who are not in a performing ensemble may still enroll and succeed in AP Music Theory. This course is offered every other year (2026-27, 2028-29 etc.).
prerequisites: Successful completion of Music Appreciation (formerly known as Music Theory), one of the ensemble classes, or instructor permission.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving. | *BHS partners with Saint Michael’s College to offer this course as a concurrent enrollment class. This means that you could earn college credit for this class, in addition to BHS credit. If a student opts in concurrent college enrollment for this course, they will need to submit a dual enrollment voucher form to Saint Michael’s. See Ms. Stein (kstein@bsdvt.org) for details and support. | Also listed on p.112 of main catalog as 'AP Music Theory' (Flexible Pathways) | Concurrent enrollment option (p.111): BHS partners with St. Michael’s College (SMC) to offer college credit for the equivalent of AP US Government, AP Literature, Honors Physics and AP Music Theory.

description: The Chamber Choir is a select auditioned group that meets weekly before school hours to sing music scored for smaller ensembles. Students will sing Soprano/Alto, Tenor/Bass, and SATB pieces. The group rehearses music from many different genres (acapella, barbershop, musical theater, madrigals, and more) in preparation for several performances during the school year. A strong commitment must be made to rehearsals and to work outside of the regular rehearsal period.
prerequisites: Audition or recommendation from Choir Director is required.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development, Curiosity & Creativity.

description: The Concert Band presents and encourages music performance at Burlington High School. The Concert Band is open to all students in grades 10-12 who play woodwind, brass, or percussion instruments. The Concert Band studies music from many different historical periods presenting diverse musical styles and genres. This performance ensemble is dedicated to the development of individual instrumental technique and large ensemble skills. Students are eligible to represent Burlington High School through music festivals at the district, state, and regional levels.
prerequisites: Successful completion of 1 year of Freshman Band
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: The Concert Choir is open to ninth grade and other new singers who wish to participate in the BHS choral program. In addition to performances, members in this group will engage in a program designed to improve their musical skills in rhythm, reading, and technical proficiency on their voice part. This course will include the study of music theory, rehearsal procedure, proper practice habits and a variety of aspects to help strengthen vocal skills. All students interested in singing are encouraged to sign up for this course, even if you do not presently sing.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Calling all string players! The Concert Orchestra is open to all students in grades 9-12 who play violin, viola, cello or string bass. In Concert Orchestra, we study and perform works from the classical genre as well as music from movies, musicals and more! In addition to instruction on their instruments, students will also have brief lessons in music history and music theory to help them become a well rounded musician. Students are eligible to represent Burlington High School through music festivals at the state and regional levels. Instruments are provided for those in need.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Digital Music is an introductory course open to all students regardless of music experience. This course is an introduction to the integration of electronics into the world of music creation. Students are taught how to utilize a digital audio workstation, to remix pre existing pieces of music as well as create their own projects from scratch. Students will also be introduced to podcasting and the art of cinema composition. Additionally, students will study composition and recording techniques used by today’s most popular recording artists.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development, Curiosity & Creativity, Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: The Freshmen Band presents and encourages music performance at Burlington High School. The Concert Band is open to all students in grade 9 who play woodwind, brass, or percussion instruments. The Freshmen Band studies music from many different historical periods presenting diverse musical styles and genres. This performance ensemble is dedicated to the development of individual instrumental technique and large ensemble skills. Students are eligible to represent Burlington High School through music festivals at the district, state, and regional levels.
prerequisites: All students welcome

description: This introductory guitar class is designed for students with little or no guitar experience. Using guitars provided by the school, students will learn the basics of playing, reading, and writing guitar music. In this course, students will play notes and melodies through the range of the instrument, learn about 20 chords, and read music in standard notation, pop chord notation, and tablature. Music will be chosen from folk, classical, rock, and popular styles.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This advanced guitar class is designed for 10th-12th grade students with experience playing guitar and reading music. Students will continue to improve their reading, writing, and playing skills. They will be introduced to playing in different positions, barre chords, transposition, and ensemble playing. Music will be chosen from folk, classical, rock, and popular styles. Students who have not taken Guitar I should discuss this choice with a guidance counselor or music teacher before enrolling.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Guitar I or teacher recommendation.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: An introduction to the art and practice of theatre, including acting, directing, stage managing, playwriting, and the various design elements (scenic (set), lighting, sound, wardrobe, and more). This exploratory course will utilize Burlington High School's state of the art performing arts space. This course provides a balanced creative and technical theater education for students of any experience level.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: The Jazz Ensemble presents and encourages music performance at Burlington High School. This yearlong co-curricular group meets twice a week in the morning before school and is open to band and orchestra members. Repertoire includes classic big band charts as well as arrangements by contemporary artists. There is a strong emphasis on jazz styles and improvisation. Students are eligible to represent Burlington High School at the Vermont All-State Festival.
prerequisites: Audition required. Auditions are open to students presently enrolled in: concert band, wind ensemble, string orchestra, or symphonic strings (exceptions for guitar and piano only).
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

course_name: Music Appreciation (Formerly Introduction to Music Theory I)
description: This course aims to deepen student’s appreciation of music through the study of historical context, music theory, and song writing. Current events, pop culture, and students' music preferences are the driving force for this course. Western Classical music will be used to introduce foundational musical concepts such as reading music in different clefs, learning scales, and basic music composition and notation. This course is appropriate for musicians at any level. You are not required to play an instrument or perform in a music ensemble.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This Piano I class meets students where they are at in their piano journey, whether that is a brand new beginner, or a student who has dabbled in piano before and looking for more experience. Using keyboards provided by the school, students will learn the basics of playing, reading, and/or writing piano music. In this course, students will learn to play songs designed for their level, chords, melodies and read music in standard notation. Music will be chosen from folk, classical, and popular styles.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

description: This intermediate piano class is designed for students with experience playing piano and reading music. Students will continue to improve their reading, writing, and playing skills. They will be introduced to playing in different keys, scales and arpeggios and further study of basic music theory.. Music will be chosen from folk, classical, rock, and popular styles. Students who have not taken Piano I should discuss this choice with their school counselor or music teacher before enrolling.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Piano I or teacher recommendation.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: The Senior Choir is open to students who like singing in mixed voices (soprano/alto/tenor/bass) and are committed to improving their vocal development. Music of all styles will be performed and studied while giving proper attention to singing technique, music reading, analysis, and evaluation. Exploration of world music will also be offered. Students who wish to play a more active part in their choral development are offered the opportunity to audition for the following music festivals: Champlain Valley District, Vermont All State, and New England Music Festivals. In addition to the scheduled performances each year, students will also be given the opportunity to perform in several Small Ensemble Performances.
prerequisites: One year of Concert Choir or recommendation of the instructor.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: Calling all advancing string players! The Symphonic Orchestra is open to all students in grades 10-12 who play violin, viola, cello or string bass. Symphonic Orchestra students will study and perform more advanced works from the classical genre as well as music from movies, musicals and more! In addition to instruction on their instruments, students will also have brief lessons in higher level music history and music theory to help them become a well rounded musician. Students are eligible to represent Burlington High School through music festivals at the state and regional levels. Instruments are provided for those in need.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Concert Orchestra or recommendation of instructor.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving, Personal Development.

description: Wind Ensemble presents and encourages music performance at Burlington High School. Wind Ensemble is open to students in grades 10-12 who play woodwind, brass, or percussion instruments. Performance repertoire will include masterworks for the wind band and advanced 20th century compositions. Emphasis is placed on independence of parts, technical proficiency, and musical interpretation. A minimum of one year’s experience in Concert Band is strongly recommended. Students are eligible to represent Burlington High School through music festivals at the district, state, and regional levels.
prerequisites: Successful completion of 1 year of Freshman Band or Concert Band.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Curiosity & Creativity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This year-long course, coordinated with Humanities English 9, will explore the themes of power, liberty, security and conflict. Our examinations of these themes will be filtered through the lens of American government and culture, and will also include global differences and impact. Students are expected to demonstrate their understanding of how our democratic republic functions and their roles and responsibilities as citizens. In addition, students examine issues and Constitutional protections connected to human rights. course_name: Ethnic Studies: A People’s History Part I
description: This course fulfills 0.5 credits of the American History graduation requirement. This is a semester-based course that provides an opportunity to explore American History through the voices that are often silenced, such as Native Americans, European immigrants, and Latinos. We aim to unpack the social, political and economic implications on America’s development on marginalized peoples in an ethnic studies approach. Our historical timeline of study is from First Contact through Reconstruction. This course has been designed and inspired by historian Howard Zinn’s book, “A People’s History of the United States.” We use both primary and secondary sources to support our learning. Ultimately, the goal is to broaden our understanding of what it means to be a citizen in the United States, as narratives and perspectives have been left unheard. In order to fully appreciate the complex history of this nation, it is vital to recognize all voices that have played a part in America’s development, including their arduous journey.

description: This course fulfills 0.5 credits of the American History graduation requirement. This is a course about America's history through the lens of labor. We will explore the role that organized labor has played in the development of the US and examine the changing nature of work, worker movements, and employment relations in the United States. This is ultimately a US history survey course that seeks to take the lens of labor to cover key moments of US history from its founding to the present day. We will explore and analyze the attitudes, ideologies, cultures, and politics of workers, labor leaders, and employers. This course will also examine how workers of different national, ethnic, racial, and gender backgrounds have experienced work and contributed to the development of unions and worker movements. Other important themes include the rights and responsibilities of employers and workers, the role of the state in the economy and the workplace, the rise and decline of collective bargaining and the New Deal order, globalization and neoliberalism, and the current problems facing workers and the emergence of new worker movements.

description: Explore the dynamic tapestry of human history in AP World History (Modern). This course delves into the intricate narratives of global civilizations from the 1200s to the present day, fostering an understanding of the interconnectedness of societies. Students will engage in critical thinking and analytical reasoning processes as they navigate through key historical events, cultural developments, and societal transformations. Embracing the thematic approach of AP World History, learners will uncover connections across time and space, examining themes such as interaction between humans and the environment, the development and interaction of cultures, and the impact of technology and innovation. The course prepares students for the AP World History national exam, where they will showcase their knowledge through essays and document-based questions, demonstrating their proficiency in historical analysis and interpretation. Immerse yourself in the richness of global history and develop the skills needed to excel in the challenging yet rewarding world of AP World History (Modern).

course_name: Beyond the Pyramids: Intro African History
description: A general survey course designed to introduce students to major themes in African history. The course focuses on colonialism and decolonization, nationalism and self-liberation, development and neocolonialism, as well as African experiences of independence and every day in our contemporary, global world. Taking a chronological and thematic approach, this course explores major themes in African history from the end of the slave trade to contemporary times. We will cover materials from North, South, East, West, and Central Africa and explore connections between Africa and the rest of the world. Discussions will explore themes ranging from gender, age, class, race, and ethnicity, and the legacies of history in “modern” Africa. The course uses a variety of primary and secondary sources, including essays, films, photographs, speeches, newspaper articles, and political documents.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Cultural Understanding and Civic Engagement; Effective Communication; Curiosity and Creativity.

description: This course reflects on the world as an intersection of economic theory, conditions and practice. Its goal is to provide each student with a strong sense of economic literacy, so that the student will be equipped both to study economics in college, as well as to make educated financial decisions in their personal life. Student interest and contributions will direct several aspects of the course, all the while reinforcing the economic ideals at its core. The course will therefore be vigorous in its study of current events, but will also rely heavily on individual students to add value to the traditional economic curriculum. Units will seek to gain an understanding of such topics as supply and demand, personal investing, scarcity, economic systems, globalization and marketing (among others). Understanding will be achieved through a variety of interactive encounters with economic issues and problems.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Cross-Cultural Understanding & Civic Engagement.

description: This course is designed to examine historical and contemporary subjects through modern film. description: Psychology is the study of human behavior and mental processes. Students also will learn how to apply some of these psychological theories to their own lives to more cogently address their own problems and to cope with the intricacies of their inner lives. Seniors are given first preference; juniors admitted on a space available basis.

description: This semester course assists students in developing the appropriate skills and attitudes to be a safe and responsible driver throughout their lifetime. Students must demonstrate and meet objectives of each driving lesson in order to pass. description: Calculus is a valuable course for students who eventually want to major in mathematics, science, engineering, or computer science. During the first part of the course, students will study limits, continuity, and derivatives and differentials of algebraic and transcendental functions. Then students apply the derivative to sketching and to problems in related rates, maxima and minima, and curvature. During the second part of the course, students learn various techniques and applications of integration. Students are required to take the Advanced Placement Examination in Calculus (Calculus AB) which is given in May of each year. Each student will be required to have a graphing calculator (TI 83 Plus or TI 84) to use. Any student that cannot acquire a calculator may be able to sign one out from the classroom for the duration of the school year. Students are required to take the Advanced Placement Examination in May.

Thus, most of our attention will be devoted to authentic application of concepts. The first part of the course covers the concepts of limits, continuity, differentiability and derivatives of a variety of functions as well as application of derivatives to optimization problems and related rates. During the second part of the course, students learn various techniques of integration and their applications. Each student will be required to have a graphing calculator (TI-84) to use. description: This course is designed to give students a firm foundation in secondary mathematics. It is a continuation of Integrated Math 1 and students who successfully complete this class will be prepared to enroll in Integrated Math 3. The topics covered include: Quadratic Functions, Polynomial Functions and Operations, Dilations and Similarity, Right Triangle Trigonometry, Surface Area and Volume, Two Variable Statistics, and an Intro to Probability.
prerequisites: Final grade of C or higher in Integrated Math 1.
fulfills_text: Math dept: One of the three recommended credits for graduation is Integrated Math.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This course is designed to prepare students for Integrated Math 3 by reteaching the necessary prerequisite skills. The units that are covered include: Systems of equations and inequalities, Quadratic and polynomial functions, Exponential functions, Rational functions, Literal equations, Single variable statistics, and Circle geometry
prerequisites: Completion of Integrated Math 2 and teacher recommendation.
fulfills_text: Math dept: One of the three recommended credits for graduation is Integrated Math.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

description: This course is the third year of an integrated math sequence. Students who demonstrate proficiency in this course will be prepared for Pre-Calculus. Units covered include: Quadratic and higher degree polynomial functions, Exponential and logarithmic functions and their application in the real world, Rational functions, and Conditional Probability.
prerequisites: Grade of B- or higher in Integrated Math 2 or Geometry and teacher recommendation.
fulfills_text: Math dept: One of the three recommended credits for graduation is Integrated Math.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving

description: This course is designed for students who have a basic understanding of arithmetic and want to enhance their mathematics skills. It is designed to give students the foundation of understanding algebraic thinking at a moderate pace. Topics will include an extensive arithmetic review, working with variables, solving equations and inequalities, proportions and probability problems. Essential material will be covered to prepare the students for Integrated Math 1.
prerequisites: Middle school teacher recommendation or successful completion of Elements of Mathematics.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This is an accelerated course designed for motivated math students with an above average interest in mathematics. The course will cover topics such as exponential and logarithmic functions, trigonometric functions, analytic trigonometry, applications of trigonometric functions, polar coordinates, analytic geometry (conic sections), sequences and series, binomial theorem, counting and probability, and the idea of limits. Students will be provided with graphing calculators to use in class.
prerequisites: Final grade of B+ or higher in Honors Algebra II, a final grade of A in Algebra II, or teacher recommendation.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Curiosity & Creativity.

description: The students in this course must have already successfully completed Pre-Calculus Part I. This course is an in-depth review of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, as well as an introduction to sequences and series. Each student is required to have a TI-83 or TI-84 graphing calculator. Any student that cannot acquire a calculator may be able to sign one out from the classroom for the duration of the school year.
prerequisites: Final grade of B+ or higher in Algebra II, final grade of C or higher in Honors Algebra II, or teacher recommendation.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Effective Communication | Catalog text appears swapped/inconsistent: the description printed under Part I refers to students who have already completed Part I, and the one under Part II describes Part I (trigonometry); copied as printed (pp.78-79)

description: This course is designed for students who plan to study higher level math or science in their academic futures. Part I of this course focuses on trigonometry, specifically the six trigonometric functions and how they are applied with right triangles, oblique triangles, and how their graphs compare when translated. Students will prove various trigonometric identities, solve trigonometric equations, and utilize the Laws of Sine and Cosine to apply these calculations to real life situations. Each student is required to have a TI-83 or TI-84 graphing calculator. Any student that cannot acquire a calculator may be able to sign one out from the classroom for the duration of the school year.
prerequisites: Final grade of C or higher in Pre-Calculus Part I or teacher recommendation.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Effective Communication | Catalog text appears swapped/inconsistent: the description printed under Part I refers to students who have already completed Part I, and the one under Part II describes Part I (trigonometry); copied as printed (pp.78-79)

description: This is an elective class for those juniors or seniors who may be concurrently taking an advanced science class or planning to pursue a college degree in a research field. Topics include constructing and summarizing single and multiple variable data, creating and conducting surveys and experiments, understanding randomness and probability principles, types of distributions (normal, binomial, geometric, student's t, chi-square), and inference (confidence intervals and hypothesis testing). Multiple software packages and presentation tools will be used and each student will be required to have a TI-84 graphing calculator. Students are required to take the Advanced Placement Examination in May.
prerequisites: Final Grade of A- or higher in Algebra II or Algebra II Honors and teacher recommendation, or final grade of B or higher in Pre-Calculus I/Pre-Calculus II/Honors Pre-Calculus and teacher recommendation.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving, Effective Communication.

description: This course integrates the review of basic math skills with practical knowledge students need to become informed financial decision-makers. Areas covered will include calculating wages, taxes, banking services, credit card buying, housing, and automobile purchases.
prerequisites: The student must have two math credits and Junior or Senior class standing.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development.

description: This course will cover mathematics material with an emphasis on money and finances. This is an applications-based learning approach that will include the stock market, modeling a business, banking services, credit cards, mortgages and loans. We will also explore automobile and home ownership, while including household budgeting. Also included will be a look at employment basics, commissions, benefits, Social Security, looking into retirement planning. The course includes a strong review of basic algebra formulas with variables, equations, functions, systems of equations, graphs and statistics. Selected advanced mathematics topics such as, piecewise functions, regression limits, exponential functions, and linear/quadratic systems are also addressed. Much of the daily computations will be spreadsheet and/or Desmos based. Students will learn how to program complex financial formulas and results. Proficiency is based on daily attitude, participation, quizzes, questions, tests, presentations, and projects.
prerequisites: 12th grade standing and knowledge of functions.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical thinking and problem solving; Effective Communication; Personal Development.

description: A semester course aimed at students who are curious about problem solving with mathematics. The course will introduce different types of mathematics that are not typically taught in high school; number theory, graph theory and probability. We will examine classic mathematics problems that sparked new mathematics into existence. Students will be responsible for taking notes and engaging on a daily basis. The final project will be student led with them answering a question of their own making while using their new mathematical models to answer them. We will be engaging in multiple levels of discussion and problem solving. Prerequisite: a strong desire to learn and solve problems with mathematics.
prerequisites: 11th or 12th grade standing
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication; Critical Thinking and Problem Solving;

description: This course is designed for those students who have successfully completed Algebra II and want to continue studying mathematics, and are interested in pursuing STEM careers at a more moderate pace than AP Statistics. Students will focus on statistical concepts such as displaying quantitative data, basic probability, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing.
prerequisites: Completion of Algebra II or Honors Algebra II
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Effective Communication.

description: This course is designed for those students who have successfully completed Algebra II and want to continue studying mathematics, and are interested in pursuing STEM careers at a more moderate pace than Pre-Calculus. Students will review special right triangles and learn the definitions of the three primary trigonometric functions, their graphs, and their applications. Students will explore properties of the trigonometric functions using TI-84 graphing calculators and the online tool Desmos.
prerequisites: Completion of Algebra II or Honors Algebra II
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Effective Communication.

description: This course blends lifelong physical activities with team activities and challenges students to be active and engaged. Students will be expected to demonstrate knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to a variety of movement patterns. Students will have an opportunity to experience many outdoor and indoor activities. The focus of a physically literate student in this course is to be able to demonstrate personal and social behavior that respects self and others. This is a proficiency based course and students are required to demonstrate proficiency in all learning outcomes.
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 1.5 credits (at least 1.0 credit must be earned in BHS PE courses)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Cross-Cultural Understanding & Civic Engagement, Personal Development.

description: This course introduces students to a wide range of individual lifetime sports that promote lifelong fitness, personal well-being, and active recreation. Through hands-on participation, skill development, and an understanding of foundational techniques, students will explore activities such as hiking, frisbee golf, badminton, pickleball, running, kayaking, and other low-impact or recreational sports suited for all ages.
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 1.5 credits (at least 1.0 credit must be earned in BHS PE courses)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development

description: In this course, students will gain the skills and knowledge needed to participate in a variety of team sports and lifelong group activities; such as flag football, basketball, handball, soccer, ultimate, floor hockey and more. Students are encouraged to be active participants while creating a learning environment inclusive for all. Students will gain self-confidence while having fun through regular physical activity.
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 1.5 credits (at least 1.0 credit must be earned in BHS PE courses)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development

description: Students will explore movement and dance as forms of lifelong physical activity. This is a non-traditional Physical Education class with a focus on understanding movement and movement patterns along with demonstrating concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and performance. Students will have an opportunity to experience some of the following activities: flexibility and stretching, HIIT, creative dance, Geo Fitness, aerobic activities, and more.
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 1.5 credits (at least 1.0 credit must be earned in BHS PE courses)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development

description: This course is designed for students who want to learn how to improve their overall level of fitness to maintain a healthy lifestyle. Students will learn technical skills to perform a variety of fitness movements and gain the knowledge to create and implement an individualized fitness program. Topics covered include: goal setting, basic muscle structure & function, improving mobility, core development, cardiovascular fitness, Olympic lifts, strength training, programming, nutrition and recovery strategies for performance. Students will be assessed on active participation, fitness logs, current events, reflections, peer assessments, goal setting, fitness testing and a final project.
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 1.5 credits (at least 1.0 credit must be earned in BHS PE courses)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development

description: Walking for Wellness encourages students to engage in structured walking-based activity and complementary wellness components (mobility, strength, nutrition, mindfulness, reflection). The course fosters lifelong physical activity habits, self-awareness of fitness and health, and the development of a personal wellness plan. The walking format provides accessibility and inclusivity for all students regardless of fitness level, while promoting alignment with physical literacy and Vermont’s wellness goals. Students will explore how walking supports physical, mental, and emotional well-being, and how to sustain healthy movement patterns beyond high school.
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 1.5 credits (at least 1.0 credit must be earned in BHS PE courses)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development

description: Students may choose this course as an independent study for Physical Education. Students enrolled in this course have some flexibility of designing a plan that fits their needs. This course is ideal for those students who thrive with the opportunity to self-direct their own learning and wish to develop their own path and personal learning plan. There will be opportunities to do just that, while there will also be prescribed assignments. In this course students have the opportunity to use outside learning physical activity opportunities and apply them to this course for credit. The focus is becoming physically literate and demonstrating the knowledge and skills to achieve and maintain a health-enhancing level of physical activity and fitness. Regular meetings before school with a teacher and submissions of work will be required for students to demonstrate progress towards meeting course goals.
prerequisites: Limited slots are available; student placement by teacher recommendation ONLY
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: Only 0.5 credit can be earned in PE Capstone.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development and Critical Thinking 52091, 52092, 52093

description: Students may earn up to 0.5 PE credit for completing two seasons of interscholastic sports team involvement at BHS. This option is available beginning in sophomore year and ending Fall season of senior year. Students will fill out the interscholastic sports credit form and successfully complete their season. The coach and PE teacher overseeing this will determine successful completion. In addition, in order for students to receive this credit there are four required assignments that all student athletes must complete by the end of their season. Communication is given at the beginning of each season regarding this information. Students are assigned to a course in Schoology to access the assignments. In order to earn the credit, students must complete all five elements listed below: 1. Participation in the sport for the entire season 2. Weekly log of activities aligned with PE proficiencies 3. PE proficiency reflection 4. Coach and Student Rubric
prerequisites: Students must earn at least 0.5 PE credit in their 9th grade yearOR be enrolled in a PE class in their 10th grade year (either semester)
fulfills_text: Physical Education graduation requirement: 0.5 credits may be earned in Interscholastic Sports in Grades 10-12; Fall only, Senior Year.
notes: Grades as printed: Grades 10-12 (Fall season only for 12th grade) | Primary Graduate Expectations: Personal Development

description: Over the course of the semester, students will explore and engage in a variety of health related topics. They will gain factual information that can be used to make informed decisions regarding their own health. Topics covered include: mental health, nutrition, substance abuse & prevention, and sexual health. All units are aligned with the National Health Standards and each unit has specific learning outcomes and proficiencies. This course is a BHS and State graduation requirement.
fulfills_text: This course is a BHS and State graduation requirement.
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Cross-Cultural Understanding and Civic Engagement, Effective Communication, Personal Development; Curiosity and Creativity.

description: In this fall semester course, students will investigate the food choices and practices of a region of our country, including: national issues such as diabetes, child hunger and heart disease. Students will plan, prepare and serve dishes related to his/her chosen area to the class. Students will also investigate and demonstrate understanding of food preparation and food science in chosen areas. The class will culminate with a holiday party for a chosen group. Unit evaluations will be class generated and include school wide contests.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Health
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Cross-Cultural Understanding and Civic Engagement, Personal Development.

description: In this spring semester course, students will investigate the food choices and practices of an international culture or country, including global issues such as disasters, war, and other catastrophes and their effect on the food supply. Students will plan, prepare and serve dishes related to his/her chosen area to the class. Students will investigate and demonstrate understanding of food preparation and food science in chosen areas. Unit evaluations will be class generated and include school wide contests.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Health
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Cross-Cultural Understanding and Civic Engagement, Personal Development.

description: This course provides students with scientific literacy in earth sciences. These areas will be explored through inquiry, discussion, projects, lab investigations, research and technology. This course will include place-based study of the Burlington area, from the ecology of Lake Champlain to the geology of Lone Rock Point. Students have the option to earn honors credit in this class by demonstrating learning of key concepts, skills, and knowledge, on identified assignments and assessments throughout the school year at an honors level; the earned honors designation will be awarded at the end of the year. This course is required for all 9th grade students. 10th grade students by teacher recommendation only. This course is not appropriate for 11-12th grade students.
fulfills_text: This course is required for all 9th grade students. | Science dept table: Required Courses - Earth Systems Science (9th grade)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication, Creativity and Curiosity, Critical Thinking and Problem Solving.

description: This full-year course focuses on Biology and biological applications and will help to improve the student’s science skills, as well as general academic skills. Students will regularly conduct laboratory investigations and complete research projects. The major biological content covered will include biochemistry, cell structures and functions, cellular energy systems, cellular reproduction, genetics, evolution, and environmental science. Successful completion of this course will provide students with the skills needed to take future science courses.
prerequisites: Enrollment in grade 10 or higher.
fulfills_text: Science dept table: Required Courses - Biology (10th grade)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication, Creativity and Curiosity, Critical Thinking and Problem Solving.

description: Biology is the study of life. In this class, students will do the following: ● Study how environmental changes drive the evolution of a species ● Use models and simulations to uncover how DNA encodes all the instructions for making living things and research how mistakes in those instructions can lead to a variety of disorders such as cancer ● Explore how the body changes during intense exercise like running a marathon In Honors Biology, students will continue to expand their proficiency in science skills such as Asking Questions and Developing Models (ESS proficiencies). Students will also be asked to show proficiency in Analyzing and Interpreting Data, Mathematics and Computational Thinking, and Engaging in Argument from Evidence. Students will show proficiency in these skills through modeling current biological concepts, engaging in scientific discussion, exploring current scientific writing, conducting labs, applying technology and simulations to expand understanding, writing scientific explanations, and completing research and projects. Students’ biology-specific content knowledge will also be assessed throughout the course using quizzes and tests. This challenging and fast-paced course will provide students the skills needed to take future honors and AP-level science classes at BHS and introductory college-level science courses in the future.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Earth Systems Science and Earth Systems Science teacher recommendation.
fulfills_text: Science dept table: Required Courses - Biology (10th grade)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication, Creativity and Curiosity, Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This proficiency based college preparatory chemistry class focuses on proficiency in fundamental chemistry concepts and skills. This course includes a mixture of classic laboratory work, guided inquiry, and experimental design. A strong algebra foundation is essential for success as it is applied to many chemistry concepts. Topics studied include: classification of matter, atoms, elements, nuclear chemistry, chemical compounds, bonding, chemical composition, and reactions.
prerequisites: Successful completion or concurrent enrollment of Biology I, Integrated Math 1 (or a higher level math), and recommendation of current science teacher
fulfills_text: Science dept table: Required Courses - Chemistry and or / Physics (10th, 11th, or 12th grade)
notes: Grades as printed: Grades 11-12, 10th Grade by Recommendation | Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication; Creativity & Curiosity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This college preparatory chemistry class is a rigorous, math-dependent science course. Basic chemistry concepts are emphasized in class discussions, labs, and independent learning. Topics studied include: atomic and molecular structure/ theory, periodic law, chemical bonding, formulas, equations and stoichiometry, chemical reactions, acid and bases, and nuclear chemistry.
prerequisites: Successful completion of or concurrent enrollment in Biology I or Biology I Honors, Algebra II or Algebra II Honors, and recommendation of current science teacher.
fulfills_text: Science dept table: Required Courses - Chemistry and or / Physics (10th, 11th, or 12th grade)
notes: Primary Graduate Expectations: Effective Communication, Creativity & Curiosity; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving.

description: This is a college-preparatory laboratory oriented physics course designed for students with strong reading, problem solving and computation skills. Topics in physics include Energy, Newton’s Laws, Gravitation, Waves, and Sound. Topics are covered using inquiry, group work, experimentation, and mathematical relationships as indicated by the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS).
prerequisites: Successful completion or concurrent enrollment of Biology I, Integrated Math 1 (or a higher level math), and recommendation of current science teache . r
fulfills_text: Science dept table: Required Courses - Chemistry and or / Physics (10th, 11th, or 12th grade)
notes: Grades as printed: Grades 11-12, 10th Grade by Recommendation | Primary Graduate Expectations: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Effective Communication.

description: This math and laboratory-based course is designed for students with very strong reading, problem solving, and mathematics skills. Students work independently and in collaborative groups to discover important concepts in the study of kinematics, Newton’s Laws, energy, rotational motion, waves, sound, and optics.
prerequisites: Successful completion of or concurrent enrollment in Biology I or Biology I Honors, Algebra II or Algebra II Honors, and recommendation of current science teacher.
fulfills_text: Science dept table: Required Courses - Chemistry and or / Physics (10th, 11th, or 12th grade)
