A GLO provides extra support and guidance as the student practices personalized learning skills. Students must have an interest to work independently. Off-site time with a community mentor is strongly encouraged.
prerequisites: Students must have an interest to work independently.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Determined Upon Enrollment; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Community Connection; Listed as separate A and B sections (910032, 910033)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: An ILO in Social Studies is an opportunity to practice and improve advanced social studies and history skills while studying a topic of choice. Students must have proven ability to work independently and be motivated by a particular area of interest. Off-site time with a community mentor is strongly encouraged.
prerequisites: Students must have proven ability to work independently.
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Civics, Economics, Geography, History; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Community Connection; Listed as separate A and B sections (909031, 909038)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: The field of brain research is exploding. In Psychology, we take the first steps toward understanding the mind boggling connections within our brains and through our bodies. Your brain exists for you to individually take action in this world, and Psychology class helps you understand why you take those actions. In class, you will help select the most recent research available to uncover the brain discoveries. You will examine how psychology is used in identity development, sports and daily life. You will leave understanding how human senses, emotions and neurological differences create uniquely wonderful human beings.
prerequisites: none, *10th graders with approval from instructor
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: History; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking, Effective Communication

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
course_name: The Middle Ages to the French Revolution
description: Students will explore the events and cultural exchanges that led to revolutions in thinking and technology. Students will examine how the Western European culture, political systems, and economies developed as a result of the revolutionary events of the 14th-18th centuries.
prerequisites: US History *10th graders with approval from instructor
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Geography, History; Transferable skills: Effective Communication, Personal Development, Community Connection

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Advanced Placement European History is a full year, one credit course that introduces students to European History and develops an understanding of the main themes in modern European history, including political and diplomatic, intellectual and cultural, and social and economic history. The course is structured so that the student can successfully prepare to take the AP European History exam in May. Students will be provided with practical knowledge of European history, practice in critical thinking activities and experience in effective writing techniques that will better prepare them not only for the AP exam but also for their future educational aspirations.
prerequisites: Any student who wishes to enroll in an AP History course must meet or exceed proficiency in Advanced level coursework. While the Humanities Department offers multiple options for Advanced level courses, the department strongly suggests American Studies as the course that best prepares students for AP level work due to its year-long structure, rigorous reading and writing load and emphasis on seminar-style discussion. Admission is contingent upon completion of summer work. Permission may be given on an individual basis by the Humanities teaching team and school counselors.
notes: Benchmark: Advanced Placement; Content proficiencies: Civics, Economics, Geography, History, Argumentative Writing; Transferable skills: Community Connection, Effective Communication, Personal Development; Listed as separate A and B sections (412040, 412041)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Sociology is a one-semester course where you investigate how social systems influence human interactions. Instead of focusing on the brain-body connection as students do in Psychology, you collaborate with classmates to analyze group dynamics. You determine how group structure, individual interactions, inherent social problems and symbolism impact each person’s choices and actions. You demonstrate your use of the “sociological perspective” to understand our global society and analyze current events. Considerable effort goes into conducting active, “hands on” research and analyzing group experiences. Collaborative participation in these activities is a key to the class’ and your success.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Civics, Economics, History; Transferable skills: Effective Communication, Personal Development, Community Connection

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Vermont History is a semester-long course that explores selected topics in the history of our home state from its first settlement by Native Americans, to the present day. While the course will follow a general chronological framework, treating each major historical period in turn, students will be encouraged to explore topics of personal interest to them in any historical period, or across several periods.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: History; Transferable skills: Effective Communication, Personal Development, Community Connection

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Advanced Placement US History is a full year, one credit course that surveys American History from the Age of Exploration up to the 21st century. The course is structured so that the student can successfully prepare to take the AP US History exam in May. Through this course, students will be provided with practical knowledge of U.S. history, practice in critical thinking activities and experience in effective writing techniques that will better prepare them not only for the AP exam but also for their future educational aspirations.

notes: Benchmark: Advanced Placement; Content proficiencies: Civics, Economics, Geography, History, Argumentative Writing; Transferable skills: Effective Communication, Personal Development, Community Connection; Listed as separate A and B sections (412030, 412031)

description: Bridge to Integrated Math is designed to prepare students for the Integrated Math sequence. Students will explore topics in number and quantity, algebra and statistics. Topics of study in this course include: exploring and communicating mathematics; simplifying expressions, solving equations and systems of equations; problem solving; coordinates and functions; proportional thinking; properties of linear functions; and two and three dimensional geometry.
notes: Benchmark: Novice; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication; Listed as separate A and B sections (709000, 709001)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Integrated Math 1 is a first level course in a core curriculum of high school mathematics. Students will explore topics in number and quantity, algebra and statistics. Topics of study in this course include: exploring and communicating mathematics; simplifying expressions, solving equations and systems of equations; problem solving; coordinates and functions; proportional thinking; properties of linear functions; and two and three dimensional geometry.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication; Listed as separate A and B sections (709010, 709011)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Integrated Math 2 is a second level course in a core curriculum of high school mathematics. Students will explore additional topics in algebra, geometry, and mathematical computation. Topics of study in this course include: quadratic and exponential functions and graphs; special triangle relationships including introduction to trigonometry.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 1; required 2.5 or above Academic and Transferable Skills grade each semester in Integrated 1
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication; Listed as separate A and B sections (709020, 709021)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Integrated Math 3 is a third level course in a core curriculum of high school mathematics. Students will explore additional topics in algebra, geometry, statistics, logical reasoning, and mathematical computation. Topics of study in this course include: sequences; exponential functions; polynomial functions; introduction to data literacy; the unit circle; imaginary numbers and special relationships in circles.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 2; required 2.5 or above Academic and Transferable Skills grade each semester in Integrated 2
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication; Listed as separate A and B sections (709030, 709031)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Money Matters 1 is a required course needed for graduation. This course focuses on the math that helps us manage our personal finances and the economic context in which financial decisions are made. Instruction will link mathematical procedures to broader economic concepts in addition to maintaining math skills. Topics covered include careers, budgets, paychecks, banking, financial pitfalls (such as fraud and scams) and credit.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 1
fulfills_text: *required course; Money Matters 1 and US Government and Politics are required in either junior or senior year to meet graduation requirements.
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Financial Literacy; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Money Matters 2 also focuses on the math that helps us manage our personal finances and the economic context in which financial decisions are made. Topics in this course include investing, housing, insurance, taxes, entrepreneurship, and vacations.
fulfills_text: Does not meet the Financial Literacy graduation requirement.
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Financial Literacy*; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Money Matters (year-long) focuses on the same topics as semester Money Matters 1 and also meets the financial literacy graduation requirement. Students recommended for this course will explore each topic listed in the Money Matters 1 course description more extensively while they continue to build their mathematics skills for their post-high school career and daily living needs.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 1, teacher recommendation only
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Financial Literacy; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Pre-calculus blends the concepts and skills that must be mastered before enrollment in a college-level calculus course. The primary goal of this course is to expand and reinforce the ability to understand, manipulate, and apply mathematical concepts. Topics of study in this course include: functions and their graphs; polynomial and rational functions; exponential and logarithmic functions; trigonometric functions; analytic trigonometry; additional topics in trigonometry; linear systems; vectors; the polar coordinate system; and a brief introduction to entry level calculus topics.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 3; recommended 2.5 or above Academic grade in Integrated 3
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication; Listed as separate A and B sections (710000, 710001)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Semester Pre-Calculus is a math course designed for students who want to accelerate their math learning after the first semester of IM3. This course will cover all of the topics of Pre-Calculus (with the exception of vectors and the polar coordinate system) plus the remaining IM3 learning targets in a semester versus a year. For that reason, this course will meet DAILY second semester. Ideal candidates for this course should have routinely met or exceeded the standards in both Integrated Math 2 and the first semester of Integrated Math 3. Students in this course should have a strong interest in completing AP Calculus or other upper level math electives before graduation.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 3A; recommended 2.5 or above Academic grade in Integrated 3
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication Semester 2 only; meets daily

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Data, Data, Data, it is everywhere! Smartphones and Fitbits can collect data continuously. Phone Apps are even created to help the user or an organization collect data. In this course students explore how statistics can be used to impact business, environmental, and personal decisions. Students will learn skills essential for understanding and interpreting statistics. We will interpret and critique statistics in the media and explore the major concepts and tools for gathering, analyzing and interpreting data. This course is a great introduction to statistics for students pursuing further education in psychology, business, education, or social sciences as well as math and science.
prerequisites: Integrated Math 3
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Statistical Literacy; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Effective Communication

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: This rigorous course is designed for students who want to continue their study of mathematics at an advanced level. Students considering a career in science, mathematics or engineering are encouraged to enroll in this course. Calculus focuses on limits and continuity as well as concepts and applications of derivatives and integrals. Students may receive college credit or advanced college placement for high scores on the AP exam given each May. AP Calculus is intended for students who have a comfortable working knowledge of college preparatory mathematics, including algebra and trigonometry. In line with the calculus reform movement, conceptual understanding will be stressed throughout the course. The expectations are similar to those of a college-level course, therefore students are expected to devote at least as much time outside of class to the course as the time spent in class. This course will meet for a full block daily during the first semester and every other day during the second semester.
prerequisites: Pre-Calculus; recommended 2.5 or above Academic grade in Pre-calculus
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Math Concepts & Skills; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Community Connection; Listed as separate A and B sections (711010, 711011); meets daily first semester

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In this course, you will explore how scientists investigate the natural world to explain the physics and chemistry of Earth. You will study the properties of matter and chemical reactions, explore forces and energy in motion, and deepen your understanding of Earth systems and resource management. Through hands-on labs and inquiry-based projects, you will build skills in modeling, data analysis, and problem-solving to explain and apply scientific ideas.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Earth & Space Sciences, Physical Sciences, & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking; Listed as separate A and B sections (1009004, 1009006)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In this course, students explore the incredible diversity of life—from the microscopic scale of cells and organelles to the interactions among organisms and their environment. Students will investigate how structure relates to function in living things, analyze patterns in animal behavior through their own inquiry-based project, and apply scientific reasoning to evaluate current environmental challenges. Throughout the course, students develop skills in data collection and presentation, modeling, problem-solving, and data analysis to gain a deeper understanding of how life on Earth is interconnected.
prerequisites: Science 9 or recommended 9th graders with instructor permission.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Life Sciences, Earth & Space Sciences, & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking; Listed as separate A and B sections (909083, 909084)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In this course, you will explore the fundamental concepts of chemistry and relate these to real-life situations and problems. You will gain an understanding of how chemists investigate the natural world by examining chemicals and the reactions between them. You will gain a deeper understanding of the nature of matter, the role of energy in our world, and how gases and liquids interact. You will also explore how chemistry relates to design and engineering, energy production, climate change, and clean air as well as potential solutions to issues affecting people and the Earth.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 or Biology & Integrated Math 2
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Physical Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking; Listed as separate A and B sections (1009010, 1009011)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In this course, you will use class investigations to explore how matter and energy interact in the universe. Potential topics covered include One- and Two-Dimensional Motion, Newton’s Laws of Motion, Conservation of Momentum, Thermodynamics, Waves, and Electromagnetism. Students signing up for this course should be prepared to work independently outside of class and meet with the teacher as needed to understand the material. After this course, students will be able to conceptually apply mathematical reasoning and scientific laws to understand the physical properties of the universe we live in.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 or Biology & Integrated Math 2
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Physical Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking; Listed as separate A and B sections (1010040, 1010041)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Students will learn selected techniques used in forensic investigations. They will apply those techniques to crime scenes and evidence analysis. The course will include laboratory exercises in evidence collection, analysis, and the application of forensic techniques in fiction.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Life Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: The purpose of this course is to give you a solid technical understanding of the major ideas in Biology. Near the end of the course, you may take a national exam that may qualify you for college credit or placement out of entry-level college courses. We will explore evolution and the molecular basis of life in semester 1. Metabolism and ecology are major topics in semester 2. Learning will occur via traditional classroom modalities and significant student inquiry in the lab. This college-level course proceeds at a fast pace and enrolled students should be prepared to dedicate at least 1 hour per night to completing assignments, reading, and self-study.
prerequisites: Earth Science, Biology & Chemistry
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Life Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking; Listed as separate A and B sections (1011040, 1011041); double block

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In Vermont Ecology, explore and learn about the Vermont ecosystem and the current environmental issues in the state. This course will focus on both freshwater aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Students will learn about the history of the Vermont ecosystem and explore the current state of Lake Champlain and feeding watersheds and the Vermont forest through hands-on environmental monitoring methods. After becoming more informed, get ready to discuss the future of Vermont and form opinions about current management and issues. Develop a plan to move our state forward.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 & Biology
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Life Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: This course will take a closer look at one of the most fascinating subjects possible—your own body. You’ll find it helpful to learn about the workings of your body to appreciate emerging discoveries in genetic engineering, to understand new techniques for detecting and treating disease, and to make use of published facts on how to stay healthy. If you are preparing for a career in the health sciences, the study of anatomy and physiology is essential. Note: Limited dissections will be a learning tool in this course, but are not required. Alternatives will be provided for students who opt out.
prerequisites: Biology
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Life Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In this course, you will use mathematical reasoning and scientific laws to understand the fundamental principles of how matter and energy interact in the universe. Learning will be done through hands-on laboratory work and exploring conceptual phenomena and ideas. Physics topics covered include Kinematics, Newton’s Laws of Motion, Conservation of Momentum, Harmonic Motion, Rotational Motion, and Fluid Dynamics. This course will be challenging and fast-paced to properly prepare students for the national Advanced Placement (AP) exam in the late spring. Taking the exam is a student choice, and not required for successful completion of the course. Advanced Placement (AP) exam scores and a record of the student's learning could provide students with the opportunity to qualify for college credit or placement out of entry-level college courses. Students signing up for this course should be prepared to actively explore material and work hard both in and outside of the classroom.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 or Biology & completed or enrolled in Integrated Math 3
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Physical Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking; Listed as separate A and B sections (1011044, 1011045)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
course_name: Environmental Science A: Humans and Nature
description: In this course, you’ll explore Earth systems and resources, the interconnectivity of the living world, population dynamics, and issues of land and water use. You’ll tackle the concepts of geology, atmospheric circulation, water resources, and soil dynamics. You’ll also gain a deeper understanding of ecosystem structures and biodiversity, as well as how these processes affect humans and the environment. Additionally, you will explore how an ever-growing human population puts pressure on natural resources. *You may enroll in this course as a stand-alone, one-semester course, or it can be combined with Environmental Science B: Energy, Pollution, and Climate Change for a complete, year-long environmental science course. **You may elect to take the national Environmental Science Advanced Placement (AP) exam if you are enrolled in both environmental science courses.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 & Biology
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Earth & Space Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
course_name: Environmental Science B: Energy, Pollution and Climate Change
description: In this course, you will explore how the growing energy needs of human populations are currently met using a variety of techniques, and you will assess the long-term viability and effects of these methods to understand their impact on the environment and human populations. You will also explore the causes and effects of pollution and global climate change as well as develop your engineering skills by exploring ways to avoid or solve these problems. *You may enroll in this course as a stand-alone, one-semester course, or it can be combined with Environmental Science A: Humans and Nature for a complete, year-long environmental science course. **You may elect to take the national Environmental Science Advanced Placement (AP) exam if you are enrolled in both environmental science courses.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 & Biology
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Earth & Space Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: This course will take a closer look at the biology of food from the farm to your dinner plate. Students will define food and explore the biochemistry of food and nutrition through hands-on explorations and cooking activities. Students will cultivate the Mt. Abe gardens and learn about the history and current practices in world food production and transport, exploring the benefits and consequences of these practices. After learning about sustainable agricultural practices, students will focus on a food-related issue and develop a plan to improve or solve the problem. Be prepared to get your hands dirty, eat some yummy food, and engage in learning.
prerequisites: Earth Science or Science 9 & Biology
notes: Benchmark: Flexible; Content proficiencies: Life Sciences & Science Inquiry; Transferable skills: Effective Communication & Innovative Thinking

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Fitness Literacy is a semester long course required for graduation and is a prerequisite for Advanced level PE courses. In Fitness Literacy students will learn about fitness concepts, such as aerobic and anaerobic capacity, strength and endurance, flexibility and mobility, body composition, the FITT principle, SMART fitness goal setting, fitness assessment, as well as a foundational movement framework, the power of fitness, and types of exercise. Students will also experience and practice many physical activities and movement forms, including group games, modified team sports, net games, target sports, individual pursuits, and aquatics, all with an emphasis on positive social interactions in physical activity settings.
fulfills_text: *required course; Fitness Literacy is a semester long course required for graduation
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Content proficiencies: Psychomotor, Cognitive, Social, Affective; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Collaboration

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: This is a new course offering for 2026-27 school year. Games-Based PE is a semester-long course focusing on active participation, sportsmanship, and fair play through games and active play. Games may include, but are not limited to: invasion games, like tag football, ultimate frisbee, capture the flag, modified soccer, floor hockey, team handball, and soft lacrosse; net sports, like volleyball, pickleball, badminton, roundnet/spikeball, and tennis; target sports, like kanjam, bucket golf, disc golf, bowling, and archery, and baseball-like games, such as modified softball and kickball.
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Psychomotor, Cognitive, Social, Affective; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Collaboration

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: This is a new course offering for the 2026-27 school year. Lifestyle Fitness is a semester-long course using walking as a foundation for lifelong fitness. Students engage in lessons that focus on proper walking mechanics, endurance building, and safe training practices. The class includes instruction on heart rate training zones and goal setting to help students monitor and improve their fitness. The walking program incorporates core strengthening, mobility, and stability exercises to support efficient movement and reduce injury risk. Lessons also cover topics such as cadence, stride rate, walking safety, and etiquette in group settings. Other class activities may include, but are not limited to, yoga, mobility training, and other non-competive low impact exercise activities.
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Psychomotor, Cognitive, Social, Affective; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Collaboration

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Beyond the Gym is an online/hybrid physical education class that enables you to complete one semester of physical education outside the traditional gym walls, while having the support of a PE teacher here at Mt. Abe. Beyond the Gym students are required to complete at least 150 minutes of exercise on their own each week, which can include participation on a sports team, working out at a gym outside school, tracking exercise in an app like Garmin Connect, Strava, or Fitbit, etc. Students will also have two or more asynchronous remote lesson assignments through google classroom each week, and the course culminates with a fitness plan project which involves creating and carrying out a personalized workout plan and reflecting on progress. Course topics include basic health and fitness, functional training, workout plan design, nutrition, and more. Periodic in-person meetings with the course instructor are required for the course orientation, summative assessments, and fitness assessment at the beginning and end of the fitness plan project.
prerequisites: Fitness Literacy and Games-Based PE or Lifestyle Fitness
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Content proficiencies: Psychomotor, Cognitive, Affective; Transferable skills: Personal Development

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Personal Fitness is a course based on exercise physiology principles. Topics of study are: energy balance, strength training, cardio-respiratory training, nutrition, body composition and fitness plan design. Students participate in and create individual and group workouts while studying various forms of fitness training and current trends in fitness. Class may meet outside the school day. Classes are currently held at Bristol Health & Fitness and include a 4-month Bristol Health & Fitness membership, while a project to construct a new fitness center at Mt. Abraham is underway..
prerequisites: Fitness Literacy and Games-Based PE or Lifestyle Fitness
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Psychomotor, Cognitive, Social, Affective; Transferable skills: Personal Development

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In Health and Wellness you will study the topics of adolescent brain development and health, stress management, identifying your values, goal setting, decision making, relationships, reproductive health, and drugs/alcohol, and addiction. You also learn about nutrition, eating disorders, and other health topics. Through research and presentations, community guest speakers, activities, and discussions you will learn in depth, accurate information you can then use to make appropriate decisions regarding these topics and your life. This is a semester-long course required for graduation.

description: Introductory Art is an entry-level visual arts class. This class will teach foundational studio art skills, techniques, and concepts using various art materials. In addition, we will learn about the elements of Art as we complete a wide variety of hands-on projects. Introductory Art is a prerequisite for several other art classes.
prerequisites: none (This is a prerequisite for several advanced art courses.)
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: This semester-long course is meant to introduce students to the basic principles of photography, including the artistic and technical aspects of photographing and editing images. In addition, this course will teach basic Photoshop skills; students will learn to adjust, retouch, and alter images after the camera has captured them.
prerequisites: Introductory Art
notes: Benchmark: Flexible; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Ceramics 1 is an introduction to basic methods of clay construction (coil, pinch, and slab and wheel). Through the construction of three-dimensional projects, students will develop knowledge of the properties of clay, hand-building methods, sculpture, firing methods and glaze application.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Jewelry Design is an engaging introduction to the craft of jewelry making/metalsmithing. Students will learn techniques used by various cultures to make jewelry. They will produce handmade jewelry using brass, copper, and sterling silver. The pieces they create may include earrings, rings, bracelets, necklaces, and pendants. Students will become proficient in using hand tools and soldering techniques.
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Ceramics 2 is a continuation of the exploration of the craft and art of clay. This class is intended for students committed to gaining independence, skill and knowledge in the field of ceramics. Students will use essential hand-building techniques as well as the potter’s wheel to create complex and expressive forms. Students will also have the opportunity to explore alternative firing methods such as pit firing.
prerequisites: Ceramics 1
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: AP Studio Art is an intensive course that addresses advanced concepts in drawing, painting and beyond. It is designed for students who want to continue their study of art at an advanced college level and who may be considering a career in art. The AP Studio Art program offers a choice of three different portfolios: Drawing, 2-D Design, and 3-D Design. In this course students are expected to perform at an advanced skill level while taking the initiative to develop their own commitments to content and personal voice. Each student designs a Sustained Investigation that focuses on a particular visual concern in which they have a compelling interest, and explores and develops a body of work. A substantial amount of work is required outside of class. At the conclusion of the course students are expected to submit an extensive portfolio for evaluation.
prerequisites: At least three high school visual arts classes or permission of the instructor.
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts; Listed as separate A and B sections (311000, 310020)

description: Sculpture is an upper-level high school course focused on the materials, methods and art-historical context of 3-dimensional artwork. This course will expand upon construction methods learned in Ceramics 1. Students will learn principles of 3-D design, such as balance, form, volume, and texture. These concepts will be explored through making sculptures in clay, cardboard/paper mache, wire, and found/recycled objects.
prerequisites: Introductory Art or Ceramics 1
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate/Advanced; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

description: Realistic Drawing is an upper-level high school class that builds on foundational drawing skills learned in Introductory Art. In this class, we will develop an awareness of basic composition and learn techniques to draw various subject matter accurately. We will learn to render things three-dimensionally using a wide variety of techniques. Different drawing media will be explored, including graphite, charcoal, ink, and colored pencils. This course approaches drawing as a learnable, teachable skill that anyone can accomplish with practice. This course is helpful for building an art portfolio and is recommended for Advanced Placement Art and Design.

By adapting these techniques to their own designs, students will produce professional looking jewelry and art using metal as the primary medium as well as using acrylic.

notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Painting Exploration is an upper-level art class that builds on foundational painting skills learned in Introductory Art. In this course, we will emphasize composition and technique through the elements and principles of design. Students will have the opportunity to work with various painting materials, creating realistic and abstract works of art. This course helps build an art portfolio and is recommended for Advanced Placement Art and Design.
prerequisites: Introductory Art
notes: Benchmark: Intermediate/Advanced; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Visual Arts

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Hendrix, Slash, Dylan. What do these great musicians have in common? They all learned how to play guitar. This class will teach you the basics of playing guitar. We’ll learn how to play those pop songs you’ve been dying to learn. Equipment will be provided, and no previous music knowledge is needed. Although this course is geared for beginners, if you want to work on reading music and filling in some gaps this course is for you.
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Sub-heading: Music

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: High School Concert Band is a year-long course that explores the different styles and compositions of concert band literature. There are school and community-related performances that showcase the achievements of the class. Success in this course will be determined by how much a student is willing to put into learning to play an instrument better. Factors that determine success include facility, intonation, tempo, interpretation, technique, tone, dynamics, rhythmic accuracy and pitch accuracy. The proficiency of these factors will be determined through written exams and applied performances. Participation in this ensemble may lead to other music opportunities.
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Sub-heading: Music; Listed as separate A and B sections (309050, 309051)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Students will be exposed to a variety of genres in choral music literature including classical, spirituals, pop, show, folk, and contemporary selections. Through the learning of this repertoire, students will develop a basic understanding of the music language in order to describe and perform the music with the composer’s intent. All students are expected to perform in all musical presentations. Vocal performance will be stressed; however, students will work to develop skills in music literacy, sight singing and historical background. Students in Chorus may audition for District and All State Music Festivals.

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: Students will learn the basic skills needed in order to read and play piano music. Students with previous knowledge will continue working to develop and maintain musical skills. A variety of methods and repertoire books will be used allowing students to work at their own level and pace. In conjunction with playing, students will also learn music theory and composition and are expected to complete daily homework assignments. This class works to maintain a balance of academic challenge and personal enjoyment.
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development, Innovative Thinking; Sub-heading: Music

description: Music influences everything it is a part of. In some contexts the music can evoke strong emotions or tell a story. This class will look at how music is chosen and how it’s used in different contexts within media. We will look at the difference between an original score versus a soundtrack. We’ll also look at how music is used to tell a story and how it can represent certain things. We’ll be doing this analysis by watching a variety of different media and analyzing the music within it.
notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated 2x; Content proficiencies: Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Sub-heading: Music

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)

notes: Benchmark: CCR; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Effective Communication, Innovative Thinking; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Sub-heading: Music

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)

The group is self driven from selecting songs to designing the show itself. Whether you play by ear or read music, Modern Band can offer you a great experience. No previous performance experience necessary but you do have to pass an audition before being accepted to the class.
prerequisites: Audition &/or permission of the instructor
notes: Benchmark: Advanced; Can be repeated; Content proficiencies: Creating, Performing/Presenting, Responding/Reflecting; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Sub-heading: Music; Listed as separate A and B sections (909089, 909090); meets before school

Second language study also provides a deeper understanding of one’s native language. Spoken by more than 300 million people around the world, French is a practical language used in diplomacy, culture, education and the arts. French 1 provides an overview of the French language, basic communicative tasks and cultural exploration of the French-speaking world. Students speak, read, write, and listen in the French language.
notes: Benchmark: Novice; Content proficiencies: Culture, Communication; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Listed as separate A and B sections (609000, 609001)

Students expand their ability to communicate using vocabulary related to family, meals, media, travel, clothing and French-speaking destinations around the world. Students examine authentic francophone texts, music, films and audio to expand their understanding of the French language and francophone cultures.

notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Culture, Communication; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Listed as separate A and B sections (609010, 609011)

notes: Benchmark: Intermediate; Content proficiencies: Culture, Communication; Transferable skills: Personal Development; Listed as separate A and B sections (610000, 610001)

su_sd: Mount Abraham Unified School District (supervisory district)
description: In French 4, students continue to develop their skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Students solidify their ability to correctly use verbal tenses and modes in French. Students read authentic francophone texts and study current issues of French-speaking societies through various sources including music, film, online media, news articles and literature. Students observe similarities and differences between their own cultures and the French-speaking world. This class is a combination of French 4 and 5 and follows a two-year revolving curriculum. We also offer the opportunity to be recognized for language learning through the Vermont Seal of Biliteracy. The Seal of Biliteracy is an honor recognizing and demonstrating a high school student’s high level of proficiency in two languages, usually English and the language of study (in our case French or Spanish). For students receiving this award, a special seal will be affixed to a graduating student’s diploma, and a medal will be provided to wear at graduation.
prerequisites: French 3; recommended 2.5 or higher Academic grade in French 3B

description: Driver Education is a partnership between students, families, teachers and the Mt. Abraham community. Each student will participate in an A.O.E. certified program that meets the current Graduated Driving Law (GDL) standards with the goal to prepare them for driving within our five-town community. During enrollment, each student is required to complete at least 30 hours of classroom instruction while demonstrating proficiency for the classroom learning targets. Concurrently, students will need to complete at least six hours of documented behind the wheel instruction and six hours of documented observation in a dual controlled vehicle while demonstrating proficiency for the in-vehicle learning targets with the teacher. To support the learning, students are required to complete at least 20 hours of documented driving with their parents/guardians as explained in the GDL using the guide book - In-Car Guide for EXPERT Habits: The Driving MIND Pocket Coach. The culminating summative assessment for every student is to proficiently complete the final driving exam. Students that are not driving during Driving Lab may be scheduled to be in the Library or a Habits of Work Learning Commons.. 11th and 12th grade students may earn unassigned time (depending on individual student needs).
prerequisites: A valid learner’s permit on the first day of class.

description: This courses is a hands-on studio course for students who like to try a little bit of everything. Screen print your own t-shirt! Try calligraphy! Design and construct your own sketchbook! Make a miniature keychain book! Design and print on paper and fabric. You will even work with clay! Students will explore a variety of hands-on art materials and methods for art making. We will take our inspiration from social media and you! Tell us what you’d like to try.

An application must be completed and reviewed with teacher approval to take the course. 35 mm camera is required as well. Prerequisite: Art 1 or teacher approval with application completed.

description: This course is a performing ensemble with a minimum of four mandatory performances per year. Concert music is selected from various historical time periods including Renaissance, Classical, Romantic, Contemporary, and Pop. Development of proper vocal techniques, with a focus on basic music elements are explored. Included with vocal and musical development are mandatory rotating group vocal lessons. Qualified students are eligible to audition for Vermont Green Mountain Music District, All-State and New England Music Festivals. Concert performances for these prestigious opportunities are held in March and May. Each spring semester the Music Department ensembles travel to music competitions and festivals; fund-raising is necessary. Grades are based on class, lessons and performance attendance. There are written exams in January and June.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School
description: Students will learn how to record music digitally and will demonstrate proficiency with the instruments and audio equipment used in popular music and digital audio production. Students will also examine popular music history beginning in the 1950s to the present, examining different genres, style periods, and artists with historical context. Student learning will be assessed using project-based authentic performance tasks, in addition to content-driven formal summative assessments.

Students will enjoy playing a variety of songs in a variety of styles. Grades are based on preparation, practice, class participation and weekly in-class performances. There are written and playing mid-term and final exams. The semester would be divided into 4 units: 1.) Intro. to music reading and basics of both instruments; 2.) Students choose keyboard or guitar to focus on for 4 weeks; 3.) Students switch to the other instrument for 4 weeks; and, 4.) Students select which instrument to continue to work on for the rest of the semester to become more proficient.

Students will broaden their own perspectives and roles as global citizens. What characteristics embody strength in facing adversity? Students will strengthen critical reading, writing, and vocabulary skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.

This course explores these questions through reading both fiction and nonfiction texts in a strategic learning environment. Students will learn strategies to build reading fluency, comprehension, vocabulary, and writing skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 English.

prerequisites: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School

Students will broaden their own perspectives and roles as American citizens. What tensions arise when the demands of society and the individual’s desire for self-development clash? What incongruity exists between the reality and the promise of the American dream? Students will strengthen critical reading, writing, and vocabulary skills. Writing strategies, vocabulary and grammar study will scaffold deeper analysis and writing skills. Prerequisite: Recommendation, MAP Scores, and successful completion of English 9 & 10 English.

Complex and diverse texts both classic and modern will be analyzed. Students will strengthen skills in reading, writing, and thinking. Do the alienated and outcast challenge or maintain the values and beliefs of their society? What do you learn about yourself and others when reading works of fiction and nonfiction? Close reading works on bolstering comprehension and analysis. Strategic writing instruction progresses through all the constructs of writing from sentences to paragraphs to essays, and provides patterns to use for improving in all areas of writing. description: This AP German Language and Culture course emphasizes communication (understanding and being understood by others) by applying interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational skills in real-life situations. This includes vocabulary usage, language control, communication strategies, and cultural awareness. The AP German Language and Culture course strives not to overemphasize grammatical accuracy at the expense of communication. To best facilitate the study of language and culture, the course is taught almost exclusively in German. The AP German Language and Culture course engages students in an exploration of culture in both contemporary and historical contexts. The course develops students’ awareness and appreciation of cultural products (e.g., tools, books, music, laws, conventions, institutions); practices (patterns of social interactions within a culture); and perspectives (values, attitudes, and assumptions). There’s more opportunity to practice and improve all four language skills as students increase language proficiency. Prerequisite: Spanish 2 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation.

The class is conducted almost entirely in the target language with the goal of improving oral and written proficiency. In order to broaden their understanding of Hispanic cultures, students will do an extensive study of Hispanic art or history and are expected to read literary works of various genres. Preparation for the SAT Subject Test and AP tests begins in this course. Prerequisite: Spanish 3 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation
prerequisites: Spanish 3 with a grade of at least a 75% or teacher recommendation

Assignments and activities connect to the AP themes and all students take practice AP exams given in class. In addition to the two AP Reading and Grammar text books, materials used include feature films, music, native speaker recordings, authentic literature and on-line newspapers. Under the teachers guidance, students will also use text and/or video chat to gain insight into the cultures of Spanish speaking countries and to communicate with native Spanish speakers around the globe. The course is offered second semester so as not to conflict with core area AP courses. It is strongly recommended that the student take the AP exam in May. description: This course is viewed as a source of civic literacy and will survey the principles, philosophies, and practices that comprise the United States system of government and law. Contemporary issues will frame conversations about the Constitution, the courts, legislative and executive branches, and federalism. In addition, a review of major political philosophies from around the world as well as famous Supreme Court cases in U.S. history will be undertaken. Emphasis is also given to the dynamics of political decision-making and the degree to which citizens participate in political processes.

Students are introduced to the teachings of Freud, Erikson, Rogers, Piaget, Pavlov, Skinner, Maslow and others. Students will apply a variety of psychological theories to various case studies and conduct hands-on research of their own design. This is a reading intensive course, designed to foster the skills needed to succeed in a collegiate setting. Prerequisite: SS1 and SS2.

school_name: Mt. Anthony Senior Union High School

Taking physics in high school is an excellent way to lay a foundation necessary for many college programs related to science, medicine, and engineering. At least 20% of the course is dedicated to laboratory experiments involving problem solving through collaboration. description: Community Based Learning (CBL) allows MAUHS students to engage in learning experiences in a community based setting. CBL experiences will fall into one of three categories: Work-Based Learning, Service-Based Learning, or Community-Based Field Study. Assignments will be posted and completed on the CBL google classroom. Work-Based Learning- Students will gain valued job skills and learn about a specific field or career as they participate in job shadowing or internships with professionals in the workplace. Service-Based Learning- Students will engage in volunteer work that focuses on service for the betterment of our community. Community-Based Field Study- Students will explore a topic of personal interest and work with the CBL coordinator and community partners to design a learning experience uniquely tailored to meet their needs. Participation in Community Based Learning is limited to 2 semesters per student. This is an important course to prepare you for your future after graduation.

description: English 9 is a course designed to provide a strong, academic foundation in literacy that will prepare students for writing, reading, and research in all high school classes. In this course students develop their skills through extensive practice with multiple forms of writing, including literary and informational text analysis, narratives, and informational writing. Readings include classic texts such as To Kill a Mockingbird and Romeo and Juliet as well as selections of non-fiction, informational texts, poetry, and short stories. Students have the opportunity to discuss and analyze their reading using both live and electronic formats. Research skills are a major focus of the course and students conduct both short and extended research products, including written essays and presentations.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: The goal of this course is to explore our cultural foundations by reading a range of culturally significant literature, examining the lasting influence of the universal themes that emerge from our reading, and considering the importance of stories and storytellers both in shaping and conveying those themes and in providing cultural continuity. The first semester begins with an examination of Homer’s epic poems The Iliad and the Odyssey, contrasted with contemporary fiction and non-fiction texts that respond to the thematic assumptions of the ancient Greeks. In the second semester, more extensive writing is included as students engage in the Making of the Artist project, in which they will explore the relationship between an artist and his or her culture in a research paper and a presentation, and as they continue to synthesize multiple texts thematically and historically. The course is designed to prepare students to meet the Language Proficiency, which assesses students’ control of grammar in various forms of writing.
prerequisites: English 9 and recommendation of English teacher; strong analytical and note-making skills.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: The goal of this course is to explore our cultural foundations by reading a range of culturally significant literature and by examining the lasting influence of the universal themes that emerge from our reading. Readings include selections from mythology and the Bible, Julius Caesar, Fahrenheit 451, and Animal Farm. In addition to these major works, there will be selections of non-fiction as part of Non-Fiction Friday, a discussion format in which students lead each other in critical discourse on relevant and engaging topics. The course is designed to prepare students to meet the Language Proficiency which assesses students’ control of grammar and sound style in various forms of writing. Through writing, students will develop techniques for the integration of primary and secondary sources, and the synthesis of the course’s overarching themes. A centerpiece of the course is the Making of the Artist project, in which each student explores the relationship between an artist and his or her culture in a research paper and a presentation.
prerequisites: English 9

description: Advanced Placement English Language & Composition is a college level course designed to further students’ reading, writing and critical thinking skills through in-depth study of the English language, particularly language used to argue and persuade (rhetoric). Students read a variety of nonfiction texts, analyzing both their meaning and the effect of the rhetorical strategies used to create that meaning. Students then learn to apply similar rhetorical strategies to their own writing. Thematic units invite students to engage in discussion and writing about issues including the role of the individual in the community, politics, education, social responsibility, and the interplay of language and culture. In order to be successful in this course, participants will have demonstrated a commitment to independent work and study as the course requires students to spend a good deal of time reading and deconstructing college-level texts as well as writing and rewriting argument, synthesis (researched-based) and rhetorical analysis essays with control and purpose. The goal of the course is to prepare students for college writing in a variety of disciplines as well as to provide an enriching experience in the study of writing and language while engaging in the world around them.
prerequisites: Junior standing, recommendation of 10th grade English teacher. Minimum of Language PBGR met. An on-demand writing sample may be requested as well as a pre-test. Summer reading and writing is required.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: America’s rich and constantly evolving literature has served to both reflect and energize the cultural evolution of our country. This college preparatory class uses a variety of texts including novels, short stories, poetry, and nonfiction to explore themes, conflicts, and beliefs that have defined and shaped the American experience. Students examine the socio-cultural and historical influences that have shaped America’s writers, American thought, and the role of the American literary voice. Writing, vocabulary study, and the development of research skills for college reading and writing are an integral part of the course, and students take an active role in shaping class conversations and the direction of study. Major texts are chosen for student interest and exploration of the following themes: American Dream/American Identity, Freedom and Oppression, The Life Well Lived, and Real vs. Ideal. Students will also fulfill the Core Values element of their PLP in this class.
notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Writing; Research

course_name: Advanced Placement English Literature and Composition
description: This course is for those college preparatory students who are ready for college-level English assignments and have a special interest in literature and writing. The course places emphasis on analysis of literature, development of the ability to read critically, improvement in writing skills through continuous practices, and the practice and improvement of critical discourse. During two periods called Boot Camp (one for short fiction and one for poetry) students will prepare essays for each class period and in addition will have many other writing opportunities. description: If you have big ideas and an interest in using technology and creativity to realize those ideas and solve problems, Computer Science Principles is for you! AP Computer Science Principles is a year-long course which introduces students to the foundational concepts of computer science and challenges them to explore how computing and technology can impact the world. Colleges consider this to be equivalent to the first semester of an introductory course for non-STEM and liberal arts majors. It is expected that all students take the AP Examination, which includes the submission of classwork in addition to the multiple choice examination in May. There is lots of partner work, so it might be fun to sign up with a friend! There are a lot of myths and misconceptions about what computer science is and isn’t. Let’s set the record straight: ● Computer science isn’t posting pictures, sending email or searching the Internet. You can use it to pursue your interests, showcase your creativity, and even make a difference in your community. ● It’s not about sitting in front of a computer alone, typing code all day (and night). It is about using one elaborate tool to solve real-world problems. ● Teamwork is often essential to finding those solutions, and each team member’s contributions are valuable to the end goal. ● You don’t have to be a math whiz to understand computer science. ● Even though this is an AP class, you do not need prior experience programming. ● Studying computer science doesn’t necessarily mean you’ll be a programmer.
