notes: One Semester, Grades 10-12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Systems and System Models; Cause and Effect

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Integrated Earth Systems is a hands-on course that challenges students to make connections amongst the various scientific disciplines while developing their observational, analytical and quantitative skills to better understand the physical world. This course examines each of Earth’s systems, the hydrosphere, geosphere, atmosphere, and biosphere, in the context of our modern environment. Many science skills such as organizing and analyzing laboratory data, taking accurate laboratory measurements, and using the metric system are emphasized and visited throughout the course. This course serves as a foundation to prepare students for future and more advanced science classes.
prerequisites: Recommendation of 8th grade science teacher
notes: Lab Included | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Systems and System Models

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
course_name: The Vermont Sustainability Project: Fieldwork, Research, and Community Action
description: The Vermont Sustainability Project is a fall semester, two period course that collaborates with VYCC (Vermont Youth Conservation Corp) and other community partners to explore the connection between Vermont’s working landscape and the ongoing social and environmental issues Vermonters are faced with. During the first quarter, students will spend most of their time engaging in activities on the VYCC campus in Richmond, learning about sustainable farming practices, health care shares to combat rural poverty, Vermont’s recreation economy and various conservation topics. During the second quarter, students will participate in many exploratory opportunities through guest speakers and frequent field trips, and will ultimately choose one or more community mentors to develop and carry out a project designed to explore solutions to local social, economic, and/or environmental issues.
notes: One Semester, Grades 11 & 12; listed under the heading 'Grades 11/12 Social Studies/Science Elective'; fall semester, two period course; a table of Science, Social Studies and English PBGRs from which one may be chosen per category follows the description | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Presentation, Collaboration (TS); Inquiry (SS); Systems and System Modeling (SCI) In addition, the second quarter project allows you to choose up to one PBGR from each category below:

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: MMU students will start their 9th grade year with a beginning look at how our world came to be the way it is. This will be done through geographic and historical lenses. Students will learn and practice the skills of social scientists and study how geography connects to the way economic, political, and cultural systems have developed, establishing connections between the ancient world and today. The Geography PBGR will be the primary driver for the course content.
fulfills_text: All ninth grade students will take the following course
notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Geography

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
course_name: 10th Grade Social Studies: Systems of the Modern World, 1750 to the Present Day
description: The world changed dramatically during the 18th and 19th Centuries, bringing in what historians describe as “the modern era.” In 10th grade history, students will explore how this new era came about, as well as the systemic shifts that make it modern. Students examine this concept of modernity through a thematic study of the new political, social, and economic systems that emerged during this period, and explore how our complex contemporary world has both challenged and built upon these ideas of modernity and progress.
fulfills_text: Tenth grade students must take one of the following courses (2020 or 2015)
notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Geography; Economics; World Cultures

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
course_name: 10th Grade Honors Social Studies: Systems of the Modern World, 1750 to the Present Day
description: See 10th Grade Social Studies description. In addition, students examine this concept of modernity through a sophisticated thematic analysis of the new political, social, and economic systems that emerged during this period, and explore how post-war and postcolonial movements have challenged these ideas of modernity and progress through a deeper analysis of data, complex texts, and inquiry. Successful students will bring a strong work ethic and curiosity about history.
prerequisites: 9th grade PBGR met and teacher recommendation.
fulfills_text: Tenth grade students must take one of the following courses (2020 or 2015)
notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Geography; Economics; World Cultures

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Advanced Placement U.S. History is a rigorous year-long course designed to offer a college-level experience. The course covers the range of American history, from pre-discovery through the present, including an overview of significant world events as they influence the development of the country. Students are expected to handle weekly reading and writing assignments on an independent basis. The Advanced Placement program culminates in a national examination in May that could possibly lead to college credit for the course. Students interested in the course should have strong motivation, strong writing skills, an ability to work independently, and a willingness to participate in discussion.
prerequisites: 9th and 10th Grade PBGRs met as well as two teacher recommendations.
notes: Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Civics,Government & Society; History; Inquiry

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: In this full-year course, students will examine the social, political, civic, and economic issues that have faced the United States from the origin of the country to the present. The course will use a thematic approach and will cover the foundations of United States government, United States economic history, the immigrant experience, expansion and conflict, social justice and reform. This is a college preparatory course that fulfills proficiency based graduation requirements in Civics, History, and Inquiry. This is a required course for all students except those electing AP U.S. History.
fulfills_text: This is a required course for all students except those electing AP U.S. History.
notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Civics,Government & Society; History; Inquiry

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: The purpose of AP World History is to develop a greater understanding of the evolution of global societies over time. The approach is an era based study of what takes place around the world at the same time. This understanding is advanced through a combination of factual knowledge and appropriate analytical skills. The timeframe is from 1000 CE to the present. Areas covered are Europe, Mesoamerica, Asia, Middle East and India. Course highlights: the nature of changes in international frameworks and their causes and consequences as well as comparisons among major societies. A thematic approach is used for this course. As this is an Advanced Placement course, it requires a high commitment on the part of the student.
offering_note: Offered in alternate years from AP US Government & Politics; offered in 2026-27 and then again in 2028-29
notes: Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: World Cultures | Note: This course is offered in alternate years from AP US Government & Politics. It will be offered in 2026–27 and then again in the 2028–29 school year.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
course_name: Advanced Placement US Government and Politics
description: AP US Government and Politics provides a college-level, analytical introduction to key political concepts, ideas, institutions, and policies that characterize the political culture and government of the United States. How does congress work? Why do we have only two major political parties? What role does the media play in influencing public opinion? What is the Electoral College and why do we have it? We will examine these and many other relevant questions regarding political institutions, processes, and behavior. This class will encourage students to become more effective, engaged citizens as they prepare themselves to be part of an educated electorate. In addition, students will complete a political science research or applied civics project. This is a college preparatory course that will prepare students to take the AP US Government & Politics Exam in May.
offering_note: Not Offered in 2026-27; offered in alternate years from AP World History; next offered in 2027-28
notes: Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Civics, Government and Society; Economics | Note: This course is offered in alternate years from AP World History. It is NOT offered in 2026–27; it will be offered next in the 2027-28 school year.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
course_name: People in Peril: Exploring Threats We Face
description: We, as humans, face many challenges in the 21st century, both domestically and globally. From climate change driven natural disasters, homelessness, and addiction in Vermont…as well as rising authoritarianism, virus pandemics and war around the world; the threats are plentiful, and in need of recognition and solution. This course is an opportunity to explore some of these challenges through personal inquiry. Students will choose a topic of personal interest, and use the semester to explore the history of, the danger of, and best solutions to address that challenge. Students are encouraged to explore these challenges through a local perspective.
notes: One Semester; Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Inquiry

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Psychology is a course in the science of human behavior. Some of the topics covered are the brain and behavior, human development, theories of personality, dreams, social influences, mental illness and research methods in psychology. This course provides a general overview of the study of Psychology.
notes: One Semester; Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Inquiry

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Students who successfully completed Psychology 1 will further explore topics in psychology such as Sensation & Perception, Motivation & Learning, Memory, Theories of Personality, and Group Dynamics. There will be opportunities to conduct mini experiments and participate in hands-on learning activities.
prerequisites: Psychology
notes: One Semester-Spring; Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Inquiry

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Do billions of dollars in aid to Africa help? How can I tell if a charity is worth donating to? Are big corporations contributing to global poverty and environmental degradation? This course will examine the efforts to develop the “Third World” through questions like these and an examination of issues like fast fashion and sweatshop labor, climate change and sustainability, corporate social responsibility and certifications, human trafficking and rights for all. Students will learn the scope of issues facing the world, grapple with the different strategies being employed, and focus on a particular area of interest to make a change. Want to help make the world a better place? Learn how!
notes: One Semester; Grades 10-12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Economics

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This is the study of human society and human relationships. This course will focus on how the discipline of sociology examines society and human behavior in social settings. The course covers the major concepts of culture and social groups, and how people are socialized by family, peers, school, and the media. It also explores the topics of crime/deviance, the criminal justice system, and race/racism. Students will be expected to question social norms, reflect on their upbringings, and examine the structures and institutions that define our society. They will also conduct sociological research on a question they want to find out the answer to.
notes: One Semester; Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Inquiry

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Economics is the science of choice: the choices people make as they seek to satisfy their wants in a world of scarcity. In Economics, we will focus on how we make those choices, both financial and social choices, and what the societal outcomes of our collective choices on national, state, and global levels. Students will explore various economic concepts and systems along with exploring economic interdependence in a globalized economy. This will include environmental impacts, poverty, global development, political relationships and more. The insights economic reasoning provide us are powerful, and can help us understand human behavior, make more informed personal choices and make sense of current events in a complex world.
notes: One Semester; Grades 10-12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Economics

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course will focus on a variety of areas of the law including Criminal Law, Constitutional Law, and Civil Law. Individual liberties found in the Bill of Rights will be covered, including freedom of speech, search and seizure, right to bear arms, and equal protection of the laws. Students will gain an understanding of how the court system operates, including trial courts and appellate courts. The course will take a hands-on approach in which students will conduct mock trials, mock appellate arguments, and a variety of role-plays. Guest speakers and field trips on various law-related topics will help bring a real world perspective to the course. This course serves as a foundation for students interested in participating in the Vermont High School Mock Trial Competition.
notes: Grades 11 & 12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Civics, Government and Society

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: We will examine the nature, development, and role of terror and terrorist groups in a modern context. This examination will compare and contrast the origins, actions, and current situations through a mix of the following movements: Tamil Tigers in Sri Lanka, Irish Republican Army of Ireland, Maoist Rebels of Nepal, White Nationalist Movements in the U.S., Left Wing U.S. Domestic Terror, and Western Asian Terror (Al Qaeda, ISIS, etc). This course will attempt to understand the motivations behind terror as a tactic. Through the study and understanding of common roots of terror activity, we will discuss foreign policy solutions that may prevent the seeds of terrorism from germinating.
notes: One Semester; Grades 10-12 | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: World Cultures

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: In this first year course, basic language skills are introduced. Students develop a basic knowledge of French language, vocabulary, grammar and culture while working on the proficiencies of Interpretive Listening and Reading, Interpersonal Speaking and Writing, and Cultural Practices.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: The second course continues the emphasis on the language skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing. Students review and expand vocabulary and grammar from French 1. We continue to develop a knowledge of French language and culture while working on the proficiencies of Interpretive Listening and Reading, Interpersonal Speaking and Writing, and Cultural Practices. The amount of French used in class increases throughout the year.
prerequisites: French 1 and teacher recommendation.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)

Students will be able to sustain conversations on selected topics using a variety of tenses. Students work towards deeper listening/reading comprehension and expanded writing skills. This class is conducted predominantly in French.
prerequisites: French 2 and teacher recommendation.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: In this course, students prepare for AP French as they show mastery of the proficiencies in their ability to understand and discuss the main ideas of both factual and abstract topics, express and support opinions and preferences, and request clarification of misunderstood information. Students read a variety of texts in modern, conversational, and journalistic French, as well as French literature. Students prepare oral and written reports, and concentrate on mastering selective vocabulary and advanced grammar. Students will be aware of and discuss current life, events, and trends in the Francophone world. This course is conducted entirely in French.

notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Global Citizenship–World Cultures

Students explore Hispanic culture through a variety of projects and instructional methods.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)

Students participate in conversation, explore art and culture and play games.

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Welcome to the dynamic and challenging world of business. This course is designed for students seeking a non-traditional classroom experience and anyone interested in taking control of their learning. Working as a member of a team you will be actively engaged in business management and challenged to relate theories to your experience. Reading, writing, and reflecting are all critical parts of this course. You will learn how to manage yourself and your co-workers in a classroom designed for risk taking. You MUST be willing to lead and should not expect to sit quietly through instruction. Students will leave this course better prepared for life after high school by immersing in a year-long case study of workplace dynamics. You will work both within and outside of your skill sets and you will learn more from your peers than you may think possible. Be prepared to challenge yourself and your classmates, and above all else come ready to think. Recommended for any student who is a passionate and excited learner. Ideal for those planning to major in Business or Psychology, or considering owning or managing a business, although theories apply to all aspects of life.
prerequisites: Junior or senior standing or by permission of teacher.
notes: Prerequisite states junior or senior standing or permission of teacher

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course will teach the basics of design and production of wood products. The course will focus on learning skills, safety, and the practical knowledge required to work with hand and power tools. Topics include: project planning, construction, finishing methods, wood technology and joining methods. The qualities of good design will be expressed by your own creative application of the techniques of woodworking.
prerequisites: Introduction to Visual Arts
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Creating art is at the core of the Introduction to Visual Arts course; no previous art experience is necessary. This one semester foundation course will introduce students to basic foundational art skills and their own sense of creativity through a variety of media and techniques. Students explore both two dimensional (flat) and three dimensional (sculptural) art forms while learning about the visual language of art.
notes: One Semester; Introduction to Visual Arts is a prerequisite for all visual arts classes that assess proficiency based graduation requirements

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Artists will learn about the process of 2D design and observational drawing and painting as projects are sequentially designed promoting critical thinking and encouraging individual expression and imagination. This course allows students to express themselves and communicate visually. As students explore this means of creative communication, they acquire more problem solving skills. Students do not need drawing or painting experience to take this course. The course explores drawing and painting from observation and imagination using a variety of media including: pencil, charcoal, colored pencils, pastels, watercolors, liquid watercolors, acrylic paint and various mediums. Artists study the characteristics of value, color and color mixing and learn about composition, space, light, and form in order to create successful drawings and paintings. A variety of drawing and painting methods will be explored.
prerequisites: Introduction to Visual Arts
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course builds upon the skills gained in the Drawing and Painting 1 class with the focus of creating more complex and unique pieces of art. Students will have a chance to work in a self-paced, independent environment with support from the instructor to help build upon skills learned in the previous term. Students will be encouraged to explore media and methods of their choice.
prerequisites: Drawing/Painting 1
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This Graphic Arts and Design course will focus on how artists use visual literacy to create dynamic works of art that are both aesthetically appealing and have compelling visual imagery that we see everyday in the world around us, from the clothes we wear, the music we listen to, the books we read, the cars we drive, and much more. By learning about how graphic designers use typography (lettering forms) as well as compositional considerations to create logos, labels, posters, album covers, etc. and combine that knowledge with how graphic artists create artwork that utilize several types of 2D media, such as drawing, painting, vinyl stickers, printmaking and silk screening on textiles, students will create several concepts and bring their ideas to a visually satisfying conclusion for a wide audience. Students will also be given the opportunity to develop an understanding of the Adobe Creative Suite programs, such as Illustrator and Photoshop. Historical context of the development of design will be addressed through presentations and projects. Graphic Design and Graphic Arts skills are transferable to other areas of a student’s education as well as many aspects of various career choices.
prerequisites: Introduction to Visual Arts
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: In Graphic Arts and Design 2, students will be challenged to build upon previous knowledge gained in Graphic Design I or Graphic Arts and Design I. Expectations of the students will be raised to create more sophisticated imagery and use more advanced decision-making around the concepts of design. By building on the skills learned in the previous term, students will be encouraged to use their graphic art and design skills to create artwork that will be used in a graphic project such as an advertisement, album or book jacket cover, etc. and also find a “client” who will “commission” them to create art for a specific project. Students will experiment with digital imaging and use Adobe Creative Suite programs and printmaking skills, such as silk screening as well as the vinyl sticker maker to create actual products. Students will also focus on creating a professional portfolio of their work and a final presentation of their learning and skill building will be required.
prerequisites: Graphic Design 1 or Graphic Arts & Design 1
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: In this course students study the tools, equipment and techniques used when working with fine metals. The students learn about the principles of design, metallurgy of fine metals, and the techniques/skills needed to create unique pieces of jewelry and small sculptures. The primary materials used in class are sterling silver, nickel, brass and copper.
prerequisites: Introduction to Visual Arts
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course builds upon the skills gained in the Fine Metals 1 class with the focus of creating more complex and unique pieces of jewelry and sculptures. Students will have a chance to work in a self-paced, independent environment with support from the instructor to help build upon skills learned in the previous term. Students will be encouraged to explore their own styles and approaches as they learn all aspects of the design process. Students will explore a variety of topics such as, forming metal with the use of stakes and hammers, chain construction, and metal finishes. The primary materials used in class are sterling silver, nickel, brass and copper.
prerequisites: Fine Metals 1
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course will introduce students to the processes, techniques, and artistry of both digital photography as well as black and white darkroom photography. Students will learn how to use both DSLR (Digital single-lense reflex) and analog 35mm film cameras. Students will learn how to control exposure manually, develop negatives, and create prints in the darkroom, as well as learn the basics of the Adobe Creative Suite, including Adobe Lightroom to edit their photographs and Adobe Photoshop to edit, layer and apply unique effects to their photographs. As they complete assignments, students will become familiar with the different qualities of light and composition tools that give images visual impact and allow photographers to express themselves. The knowledge and skills they gain in class can be easily transferred to other editing programs. With each project, students will build confidence in their photographic ability to take well-composed images and in their expressive creativity by developing photos in both the ‘digital darkroom’ and a ‘real darkroom’. Historical context of the development of photography will be addressed through presentations and projects. With parental permission, students may sign out cameras through the library.
prerequisites: Introduction to Visual Arts
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course is designed to give students advanced instruction and experience with both DSLR and analog 35 mm film cameras. Students will challenge themselves to shoot in difficult lighting situations using flash, making more refined prints, and manually manipulating their prints in the darkroom for black and white film, as well as using Adobe Creative Suite to edit their digital photographs. Photo assignments at this level are presented as “visual problems” to be solved using the skills and techniques mastered in Photography I. Students will be challenged to use their photographs as modes of expression and communication, and will often be free to choose their own subject matter and artistic approach. This course is also designed to cater to the student who would like to work more in-depth from the rest of the class and will have independence but would coincide with the curriculum. Students may sign out cameras in the library for the semester.
prerequisites: Photography 1 or Darkroom Photography 1 (or with permission from the instructor -- Digital Photography)
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Pottery I is a course that focuses on the art and skills of working with clay, various pottery tools, and glazes. Pottery I students will learn a basic vocabulary for the medium in order to build their artistic literacy within a relaxed, creative, and productive learning environment. Historical context of the development of design will be addressed through presentations and projects in order for students to gain a deeper understanding of the medium as well as an appreciation for this ancient art form. Students will become proficient in hand building as well as have a chance to learn how to use the pottery wheel. Developing craftsmanship and an aesthetic eye are two of the goals.
prerequisites: Introduction to Visual Arts
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: Pottery 2 is a course for students who have become passionate about the art of ceramics. Students will have a chance to work in a self-paced, independent environment with support from the instructor to help build upon skills learned in the previous term. Both handbuilding and pottery wheel techniques will be encouraged, and students will be supported to take risks with their learning in a relaxed, creative, and productive learning environment. Pottery 2 students will also be required to study a potter or a ceramicist of their own choosing in order to build on their knowledge of this artform and to be inspired in their own art making.
prerequisites: Pottery 1
notes: One Semester | Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course is intended for motivated art students who are willing to devote considerable time and effort to the development and submission of an Advanced Placement Studio Art portfolio to the College Board. During the fall, the artists will experiment with a variety of approaches and media to show evidence of a breadth of experiences. In the process, the students’ artwork should acquire a sense of quality and variety. AP artists will also begin to develop a concentrated focus on individual artistic concerns. In the spring, students will continue this in-depth exploration of a specific visual idea. Substantial time will need to be spent on work outside of the classroom in order to create the quantity and quality of work necessary for an impressive AP portfolio. Participation in discussing and viewing students’ and masters’ work will be mandatory.
prerequisites: Completion of two first level visual art courses or portfolio review performed by the teacher
notes: Proficiency Based Graduation Requirement Assessed: Artistic Literacy; Reflection and Critique

su_sd: Mount Mansfield Unified Union School District (supervisory district; Chittenden East SU dissolved)
description: This course is a performing group with special emphasis on the developing musician. Students will learn and practice basic skills such as sight-reading, intonation, rhythm, counting, scales, arpeggios and a wide variety of repertoire. description: This course is for the student who would like to learn about all facets of living a healthy life. These are places around the world that have a concentration of healthy populations that live well into their 80’s, 90’s, and have a dense number of centenarians! description: This course is outdoor oriented with most days spent outside in all types of weather. Writing assignments take place atop the tallest mountains and looking out over the best vistas of the Northeast Kingdom. Reading assignments often take place in hardwood forests. This course runs in tandem with Adventure PE, a physically demanding outdoor PE course. The reading material provides the learner a level of insight into the mind and psyche of the world’s greatest explorers and adventurers that can only be gleaned by reading firsthand accounts and well-constructed retellings by the world’s greatest writers of nonfiction. Read about adventures to the world’s highest peaks, its frozen wastelands, its deserts, and its vast oceans. Read what kills even the most skilled and bravest adventurer. Read what it takes to survive. In addition to these texts, students read magazine articles published by the leaders in exploration written by the most skilled authors of our time. Students learn to record, journal, and construct written accounts of their own experiences and encounters gained during their enrollment in the Adventure PE Course – a high-level canoeing, kayaking, mountain biking, and backcountry skiing and snowboarding physical education course for juniors and seniors enrolled in either the Career Center or the High School.

description: This course focuses on the genre of poetry and song lyrics. Students will read, listen to, analyze, discuss, and write about American poems and songs. Both songs and poetry are artistic expressions that reflect the diversity of American culture and Americans themselves. Common themes such as the American Dream and the conflict between the individual and the community are explored. Through a variety of important voices, this class ultimately asks students to reflect on their learning and discover for themselves what it means to be an American, how that perception may differ from those around them, and how understanding this can lead to unity and progress. Some commonly taught authors and artists include: Edgar Allan Poe, Taylor Swift, Walt Whitman, Emily Dickinson, Tupac Shakur, Langston Hughes, Maya Angelou, Robert Frost, and Katy Perry. Students will study poetic language, figurative language, and theme. The culminating project, a research presentation or paper, will be based on a chosen song or poem selected by each student.

description: This course introduces students to the art and analysis of cinema through the close examination of movies from various decades and genres. Through observation and discussion, students will learn to “read” films by developing a critical eye for semiotics (the interpretation of signs and symbols), narrative construction, cinematography, and mise-en-scène (the setting of a scene). They will become active participants in the movie-watching experience by developing the skills to recognize, analyze, evaluate, and enjoy movies as a form of art and communication. This course is writing intensive. Students will examine various filming techniques and study the effective use of genre, character building, dialogue, plot, theme, motif, and symbolism. They will evaluate each movie on a 5-star scale and write blog-style reviews. They should also expect to write at least four academic papers using specific critical lenses and to craft several creative projects. **Parent/Guardian signature required if under 18. Film List: It’s Such a Beautiful Day, Casablanca , A Ghost Story, Parasite, Everything Everywhere All at Once, Arrival, The Grand Budapest Hotel, Fantastic Mr. Fox, Moonrise Kingdom, The Great Gatsby, Interstellar, Dunkirk, Aftersun, Napoleon Dynamite, Midnight in Paris, Arrival, One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, True Grit, Knives Out , Bonnie and Clyde, The Maltese Falcon , and The Batman.

description: In this engaging and thought-provoking English class, students will delve into the world of memoirs, a literary genre that blends personal reflection with storytelling. Discussions will focus on understanding the unique power of memoirs to reveal deeper truths about the human experience. Students will also engage in writing their own memoirs, reflecting on significant moments in their lives, and will learn how to craft compelling, authentic narratives. description: “Education Through Adventure and Service.” This course is outdoor oriented with most days spent outside in all types of weather. Using a chronological framework, a thematic approach and an arts focus, this course begins with the growth of the United States from the American Civil War and Southern Reconstruction through to the conclusion of the Cold War. The course is designed to follow the major themes, ideas, politics and historical events in US history while making connections to its current realities in order to understand the effect history has had on our everyday life. description: There are many ways to examine the history of the United States—in this course, we will put women at the center of the story. This course is a survey of the history of women in the United States from 1870 to the present. It examines the significant cultural, economic, and political developments that shaped the lives of American women, but places gender at the center of the historical analysis. The course also stresses the variety of women’s experiences, acknowledging the importance of race, ethnicity, and class in shaping female lives. We will discuss women’s political and social organizations, daily lives, economic roles, and the various ways in which gender roles have been constructed and received. The course traces a number of different interrelated themes from the late 18th century to the present: the changing conditions and ideas about unpaid housework and paid work; relations between different groups of women and the way relations of power have shaped these interactions; the ongoing political struggle to gain increased civil and political rights; and changing notions of "proper" roles for women. We will consider which ideas and assumptions within American culture have changed and which have stayed the same, and how these cultural factors have related to the material conditions through which people experience their daily lives. Finally, we will seek to understand who has gained and who has lost from these changes and continuities.

description: This course focuses on the major trends, events, and ideas that have shaped the world from ancient times to the present. Through analysis of evidence (especially primary sources), argument development, inquiry, and looking at history through multiple perspectives, students will gain valuable critical thinking skills and have a better understanding of their place in the world. In addition to class activities, students will be expected to complete a significant amount of work independently.

description: Semester 1 – Movement and Forces: develop a qualitative and quantitative understanding of how to describe and predict the motion of everything from human runners to thrown objects and even celestial objects. Then discovering what causes changes in these motions, and what happens when these objects collide. While developing your scientific skills including observation, modeling including the use of mathematical equations and simulations, and the development of scientific experimentation. Semester 2 – Conservation and Waves : develop a comprehensive qualitative and quantitative understanding of the principles of energy and momentum, specifically how their conservation can be used to describe the interactions between object and their position in our world. Then using this to observe cyclic changes in object such as springs, sound and light. Concurrently students will continue to develop experimental skills including developing techniques to maximize accuracy in experimentation, evaluating scientific arguments, design solutions and assess information from various sources to determine their validity.

Through this course, students will study various literary genres to help develop cognitive skills and abilities to think, analyze, organize, and express their ideas clearly and effectively. Throughout the year we will explore the writing processes and academic literacy skills which will include interpretation, comprehension, analysis, and evaluation of literary and informational texts. Attention to grammar and conventions of standard written English are a “must” in this class. The class will comprise a variety of short stories, novels, and supportive non-fiction to help shed light on the importance of the literary experience.

Students will also write in a variety of modes, honing their planning, revising and editing skills on essays and short timed-writes. Vocabulary and literary term development are woven into each unit.

description: Students in this course will acquire a foundation of knowledge to make decisions while driving that will ensure their safety and the safety of others on the roadway. The Driver Education Course is a decision-making process. Students will become familiar with Vermont motor vehicle laws, and learn to drive and manage their motor vehicle in various environments including city, rural and interstate driving. The course will cover the effects of drug use on the driver and the consequences of negative choices related to a driver’s personal health and safety. To satisfactorily complete the driver education course, and meet the State Requirements, a minimum score of 80 must be achieved on the road test and students are required to earn a minimum overall average of a 3.0 for Proficient in the classroom content. Students must also meet the minimum State Requirement of attendance at 30 hours of classroom sessions and 6 hours of guided behind the wheel instruction and 6 hours of observation instruction. In order for the student to satisfactorily complete the course, they must pass both the classroom and driving components. The intent of Driver Education is to help students develop knowledge, skills, attitudes and habits that can serve them for a lifetime of driving and enable them to become responsible drivers who are committed to embracing a low-risk driving style, skill and mindset.
prerequisites: Sophomore standing, age of at least 15 and in possession of a Vermont Learner’s Permit. *Students must provide the School Registrar, Amy Klinger with their official Vermont Learner’s permit prior to registering/requesting this course*The paper receipt of testing is not adequate to enroll. You need to have access to a responsible, sober, licensed 25+ years aged driver who will drive with you throughout the course. It is highly recommended that you have a minimum of five hours of driving time before registering for the course.

description: This class explores critical aspects of personal well-being and responsible decision-making. Students will delve into developing healthy habits and routines that promote physical, emotional, and mental wellness. The curriculum also addresses substance misuse prevention, fostering an understanding of mental health challenges, and strategies for seeking help. Additionally, the course covers sexual health and identity, emphasizing respectful and informed decision-making. Finally, students will learn about building positive relationships and effective communication skills to navigate social interactions and support networks. This comprehensive approach equips students with essential knowledge and skills to lead healthy and balanced lives.
fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Health

description: Students will explore the concept of mental resilience and strategies for developing strong psychological fortitude. The curriculum will cover topics such as stress management, coping mechanisms, and building emotional intelligence. Students will learn practical techniques to enhance their ability to navigate challenges, setbacks, and pressure effectively. A key component of this course will involve studying individuals who have conquered adversity and demonstrated remarkable resilience. By examining the stories and experiences of resilient individuals, students will gain insight into the characteristics and behaviors that contribute to mental toughness. Through discussions, activities, and real life scenarios, students will have the opportunity to draw inspiration and learn from these role models. Additionally, the course will address the importance of mindset, self confidence, and positive thinking in fostering mental toughness. By the end of the course, students will be empowered with the tools to build and maintain mental toughness, enabling them to face adversity with confidence and resilience in their own lives.
prerequisites: completion of Health 1
fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Health

description: In this class, students will explore the complex interplay between substance abuse, criminal behavior, and public health outcomes. The course will cover the impact of substance misuse on individuals, families, and communities, including the correlation between substance abuse and crime rates. Students will examine public health strategies aimed at prevention, intervention, and treatment of substance use disorders. Additionally, the curriculum will address the legal and ethical dimensions surrounding substance abuse, including policies and interventions designed to mitigate its societal impact. Through discussions, case studies, and research projects, students will gain a deeper understanding of this critical intersection and develop insights into promoting healthier communities and reducing harm related to substance abuse and crime.
prerequisites: completion of Health 1
fulfills_text: 0.5 credit in Health

Our mission is to cultivate a cohort of informed and passionate health advocates who actively contribute to creating positive change. Through a blend of data analysis and design thinking, students will develop the skills needed to address health challenges creatively, collaboratively, and effectively.

Students will benefit from comprehensive resistance training and cardiorespiratory endurance activities. Students will learn the basic fundamentals of strength training, aerobic training, and overall fitness training and conditioning. The course includes lecture and activity sessions both indoors and outdoors. Students will be empowered to make health enhancing choices, meet challenges, and develop positive behaviors in fitness, wellness, and movement activity for a lifetime.

With hands-on activities, students will learn practical culinary skills and techniques,and how to prepare healthy and delicious meals. Additionally, the course offers a wide variety of fitness activities, such as strength training, cardiovascular exercise, and endurance training, among others. The class encourages a lifetime approach to health and wellness, aiming to promote good habits that students can carry into their adult lives.

description: This Physical Education course focuses on leadership, mentoring, and teaching through physical activity. High school students will design and lead engaging games and activities for middle school students during lunch or recess periods. Throughout the course, students will gain hands-on experience in planning, organizing, and facilitating group activities while developing communication, coaching, and leadership skills. This course is ideal for students interested in working with youth, pursuing coaching, or taking on leadership roles in camp or recreation settings.

This course serves as a stepping stone into Algebra. Designed to establish a foundation, it delves into essential mathematical concepts crucial for success in higher-level algebraic studies. The curriculum topics include, including algebraic expressions, integers, equations, decimals, fractions, exponents, ratios, proportions, percents, area, and graphing. Through comprehensive exploration, this course equips students with the necessary skills and knowledge to confidently transition into the study of Algebra and beyond.

This course is recommended for all students. Algebra 1 course topics include solving linear, absolute value and exponential equations and inequalities, solving systems of equations using a variety of methods, an introduction to the study of functions and function notation, graphing and interpreting linear, absolute value, quadratic and exponential functions, and using these functions to model real world applications.

description: This course is recommended for all students. Geometry course topics include; angles and angle pair relationships; parallel lines and transversals; perimeter and area of polygons and circles; similar and congruent triangles; the Pythagorean Theorem and right triangle trigonometry; and other properties and theorems related to circles, quadrilaterals, and other polygons.
prerequisites: successful completion of Algebra 1

description: This course is recommended for all students. Algebra 2 includes the study of right triangle trigonometry, quadratic and higher degree polynomial functions, and exponential and radical functions. Each family of functions is used to model data and the students practice writing, factoring, solving, evaluating, graphing and transforming the functions.
prerequisites: successful completion of Algebra 1

description: This course is recommended for students who plan to major in mathematics or science related fields. Topics in the course include complex numbers, rational and discontinuous functions, asymptotes and basic limits, analytic geometry, logarithmic and exponential functions, operations on functions, periodic functions, trigonometric identities, and probability.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Algebra 2 or recommendation of teacher

description: AP Calculus AB is an advanced mathematics course that explores the fundamental concepts of change, limits, and the analysis of functions. Students will develop a deep understanding of rates of change using derivatives and learn to apply definite integrals to model net change in various real-world contexts. Through the study of limits, students will transition from discrete models to continuous functions, gaining insight into key calculus principles such as continuity, differentiation, and integration. The course emphasizes the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, highlighting the essential relationship between differentiation and integration. By analyzing the behaviors of functions, students will connect calculus concepts to solve problems across multiple disciplines, preparing them for further studies in mathematics, science, and engineering.
prerequisites: Successful completion of Pre-Calculus

description: The purpose of this course is to gain an understanding of statistical principles. You will learn how to collect data (including simple sampling and experimental designs), summarize data using graphical and numerical techniques, examine data for patterns and relationships, and analyze data so you can draw valid and appropriate conclusions. You will also interpret and judge statistical information, including information embedded in computer output. You will focus on effectively presenting statistical information to general audiences. This class is offered with a dual enrollment option through the Vermont State University system. Full year course - alternating with Personal Finance.

description: When will you use this math? Everyday for the rest of your life! How much money do you hope to make? What can you realistically expect your lifestyle to be like? Have you planned for your retirement? This course will explore how the decisions you make will affect your financial security and status. You will create a model for your life which will include choosing a career, making sure you are qualified, meeting your living expenses, taking on debt and paying it off over time, and saving in order to retire with enough wealth to sustain you in your senior years. After successfully completing this course students will be better equipped to make the important choices and avoid common pitfalls involved in living in our modern economy.

Math Lab is a supportive, hands-on course designed to strengthen students’ understanding of core mathematical concepts through interactive exploration and personalized instruction. This course is ideal for students who need additional time and strategies to grasp foundational math skills or want to deepen their problem-solving abilities. In Math Lab, students will: ● Reinforce topics from their regular math classes (Algebra, Geometry, etc.) ● Engage in guided practice, collaborative problem-solving, and real-world math applications ● Receive targeted support based on individual learning needs ● Use technology, manipulatives, and visual models to explore concepts in depth ● Develop confidence and independence in mathematical thinking

description: General Chemistry is an inquiry-based course that examines matter and the changes it undergoes. Experiments and activities are used to introduce concepts including the structure of atoms and chemical compounds, the relationships among the elements on the periodic table, chemical and physical transformations, and the measurement and calculations of chemical quantities. Students will make connections between Chemistry concepts and the world around them, exploring real-world applications of the topics they explore throughout the course. Students who complete this course will develop an understanding of interconnections among the sciences, technology, society, and the environment. This course will prepare students for a college-level Chemistry lab course.

This course will involve discussion, laboratory activities, projects, and dissections, and will source textbook material, models, and clinical studies as resources for gaining knowledge and experience with the concepts. Students who are interested in pursuing medical or veterinary careers are encouraged to take this course.
prerequisites: Biology AND 2 years of math
fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course

description: This college-level course is an introduction to the study of life, including cells, organisms, ecosystems, and evolution, and the skills of a biologist. We will take a deeper dive into topics introduced in 10th grade Biology, and explore additional topics and real world applications of biology concepts. This course will include lecture and laboratory components, and will move at a fast pace with in-depth exploration of topics; as such, students will be expected to meet a high standard of engagement in this course, both in and outside of the scheduled class period. This is a dual-enrollment course and students can receive 4 college credits towards a Biology Lab course upon successful completion of the course (per VTSU Science department expectations).
prerequisites: Biology AND and 2 years of high school math
fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
offering_note: Offered as needed in place of VTSU EnvSci; dual enrollment courses offered on a rotating basis
notes: Students can receive 4 college credits towards a Biology Lab course

description: This course explores the environment and solutions to environmental problems. Students will explore fundamental concepts in physical and ecological processes that shape our environment, and the role human civilizations have in shaping the environment. Emphasis is placed on examining solutions to current environmental problems including aspects of soil, water, and air pollution, ecosystem services, biomimicry, environmental toxicology, and more. Central to this course are hands-on labs, field studies, and student-designed projects. This is a dual-enrollment course and students can receive 4 college credits upon successful completion of the course (per VTSU Science department expectations).
prerequisites: Biology AND 2 years of math
fulfills_text: 11th/12th grade: Physical Science course OR Life Science Course
notes: Not offered 2026-27; students can receive 4 college credits

description: This semester class is an opportunity for students to explore the science of their everyday lives and the world around us. The course will integrate natural and physical sciences through topics like consumer chemistry, biomimicry, science in history, citizen science, climate & sustainability, and more. Students will build their investigative, lab, and communication skills as they engage in hands-on and project-based learning, through both collaborative and independent learning opportunities. If you are naturally curious about the everyday world around you, this class will allow you the opportunity to discover some of the science behind your wonders.
notes: Science Electives - Offered beyond the suggested progression of courses

description: This course is intended to equip students with a good understanding and appreciation of U.S. History from the Civil War to the present. Key themes include: domestic politics and policies; foreign policy and America’s changing role in the world; race and minority issues; our changing Constitution; and the interaction of citizens and government. Building students’ critical reading and content area writing skills will also be emphasized.
fulfills_text: Required to Graduate

description: This course will cover world history from prehistory to the present. Units include the Neolithic Period, Ancient World, Medieval Period, the Renaissance, the Enlightenment, the Age of Revolutions, the Industrial Revolution, the Age of Imperialism, the World Wars and the Holocaust, the Cold War, and Globalization. Major historical figures like Gandhi, Mao, and Luther will be spotlighted, as well as key events and inventions that reshaped the world. Changing systems of government, economics and political philosophies will also be examined. This hands-on learning class will emphasize critical reading and thinking skills, essay writing, and classroom discussion.

This seminar course is geared towards mastering the basics of college level World History and preparing students to pass the AP World History exam in the spring for college credit. Students should expect to do independent reading and writing at the college level and engage in class discussions to heighten understanding. The course surveys major themes in world history from 1200 C.E. through the present.
notes: **Teacher permission encouraged

description: Welcome to the exciting world of Government, Politics, and Economics. Yes, I did say exciting. Why, you might ask? It is because everything you and I think of as important and interesting in your life (sports, music, fashion, cute girls/boys, hanging with your bro’s) can all be connected to something in Government, Politics, and Economics. But that’s not all. Oh, no that is not all. It also includes such big concepts as warfare, values, law, punishment, independence, among many others. Over the course of the year we will study complex ideas like: what is the best form of government, what is the social contract, what are the rights and responsibilities of a citizen, what is wealth, how should we spend it, and some more direct applications: what do the democratic and republican party stand for, what does a town manager do, should a city build a stadium for a sports team, and many, many more. Hold on to your hats, you will be ready to step out of this course and become the active, informed citizen that our founders envisioned.

The Advanced Placement program in United States History is designed to provide students with the analytical skills and factual knowledge necessary to pass the Advanced Placement exam for college credit. Students will learn to access primary source materials - their relevance to a given interpretive problem, their reliability, and their importance - and to weigh the evidence and interpretations presented in historical scholarship. The course covers pre-European settlement and exploration of the New World to the present. The course culminates with the Advanced Placement Examination in United States History in the spring. This course is designed to complement the AP Literature syllabus.
notes: **Teacher permission recommended

description: Humans are storytellers. From our earliest ancestors we have filled our history with different myths and stories to give meaning to our lives. Over the past 150 years we took these stories that were told through verbal and written mediums and changed this to a visual one. This essential course follows the development of the medium of the moving image. We will explore the development of movies from short, silent oddities to the blockbusters of the modern day. Students will watch critically how movies have changed to both reflect and shape the world around them. With the skills and knowledge of the medium of film that you develop will change how you watch them. If you like movies you’ll never watch them quite the same way again.

For those students who enjoyed Film Studies I or who are more interested in the creative process behind making a film. In this exciting course we will not only continue our study of great films we’ll focus on the actual process. Ranging from screenplays, filming and editing students will adopt some of the techniques we examine through study and film to create their own movie.

This course will introduce students to the basic tenets of psychology. This course grapples with such complex issues as the nature of mankind, the impact of our subconscious, human development, psychological disorders and their treatments. Designed as an introductory survey course, we will take a world-wide run through the basics of psychology with emphasis on the major theories and theorists of psychology, how our psychological profile changes over our lifespan, the link between our body and brains, the process of learning, social psychology, psychological disorders, their diagnosis and treatment and the major motivators in life.

Introduction to sociology is a riveting course that is a perfect complement to psychology. Sociology focuses on the interplay of people in group settings. The course will study the development of the field, including some of the leading theorists. Key units focus on social inequality: including race, gender, and class, social institutions: including family, education, and government and how they function and the dynamics of social change.

World Religions is designed to provide students with an introduction to the diverse and complex religious traditions that exist across the globe. Throughout the semester, students will explore various religious beliefs, practices, and rituals of major world religions such as Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism, and Judaism. The course aims to foster a greater understanding and appreciation of the role of religion in shaping cultures, societies, and individuals. Additionally, students will examine the historical and social contexts that have influenced the development of religions, as well as current issues and challenges faced by religious communities around the world. By the end of the course, students will have gained a deeper understanding of the diversity and complexity of religious traditions, and will be better equipped to engage with and respect individuals from different religious backgrounds.

In this dynamic class on current events, students will engage with the ever-evolving landscape of global affairs, exploring the latest developments, controversies, and trends shaping our world. Through lively discussions, critical analysis of news articles, and multimedia presentations, participants will deepen their understanding of pressing issues spanning politics, economics, culture, and technology. From geopolitical tensions to social movements, from breakthrough scientific discoveries to emerging challenges, this course offers a comprehensive and insightful examination of the contemporary world, empowering students to become informed and active global citizens.

Civics class will introduce students to the foundations of government, citizenship, and civic responsibility. Students explore how local, state, and federal governments function, examine the rights and responsibilities of citizens, and analyze current events and public policy. Through discussion, debate, and real-world connections, the course encourages students to think critically, engage respectfully with different perspectives, and become informed, active participants in their communities.

Cartography & Culture is an engaging high school course that explores the powerful relationship between maps and the people who create and use them. Students learn the fundamentals of map-making while examining how geography, history, and cultural perspectives shape the way places are represented. Through hands-on projects and analysis of maps from around the world, students develop skills in spatial thinking, data interpretation, and critical analysis. The course encourages students to question bias in mapping, understand diverse worldviews, and create their own maps that tell meaningful stories about communities and cultures.
notes: Appears at the top of the Visual Arts page (page 38) but follows the Social Studies listings

description: This introductory course provides students with a comprehensive foundation in visual art through hands-on exploration of multiple media, including drawing, painting, printmaking, photography, and introductory three-dimensional work. Students will develop technical skills while strengthening their understanding of the Elements of Art and Principles of Design. Emphasis is placed on observation, composition, color theory, creative problem-solving, and experimentation with materials and processes. Through studio projects, critique, and reflection, students will build confidence in their artistic abilities while developing both technical proficiency and thoughtful visual expression.

Advanced Studio is a choice-based course designed for students who wish to deepen their artistic practice and explore more independent, self-directed work. Students will develop projects using a variety of media, which may include experimental painting, printmaking, book arts, photography, sculpture, mixed media, and installation. Emphasis is placed on concept development, material exploration, and intentional artistic decision-making. Through project proposals, critique, and reflection, students will strengthen their technical skills, refine their personal voice, and learn to communicate ideas through visual form.
prerequisites: Foundations of Visual Art (or teacher recommendation)

description: This introductory course explores the fundamentals of ceramics, focusing on the techniques used to create three-dimensional forms. Students will develop skills in the three core hand-building methods: pinching, coil construction, and slab construction. Through the creation of both functional and sculptural pieces, students will learn to shape, refine, and decorate their work using various surface treatments and glazing techniques. Emphasis will be placed on craftsmanship, creativity, and personal expression as students gain confidence in working with clay and develop their own artistic approach to ceramic design.

This advanced ceramics course builds upon the foundational skills learned in Ceramics I, challenging students to refine their craftsmanship and deepen their artistic problem-solving abilities. Students will further develop their proficiency in pinching, coil construction, and slab construction, pushing these techniques to create more complex and sophisticated forms. In addition, Ceramics II introduces wheel throwing while allowing students to explore new approaches to ceramic design. Emphasis will also be placed on surface treatment, glazing techniques, and a deeper understanding of kiln firing and loading. Through hands-on practice and creative exploration, students will expand their technical skills, artistic expression, and knowledge of ceramic processes.
prerequisites: Ceramics I

description: This course encourages students to move beyond traditional painting by combining drawing, painting, printmaking, collage, and textural processes to create layered and expressive artwork. Students will experiment with acrylic paint, mixed-media materials, unconventional tools, and surface treatments while exploring abstraction, personal symbolism, and contemporary approaches to image-making. Emphasis is placed on creative risk-taking, material experimentation, and developing a personal visual language through process-driven work.

Russian Exploratory is for students who would like to learn some Russian and have fun with language learning that is very different. Students will learn the Cyrillic alphabet, lots of fun vocabulary and also learn about Russia as a nation. We will also watch the series Chernobyl to learn about the explosion of the nuclear power plant in Chernobyl. And we will learn two songs!
notes: Semester One; Elective

description: Spanish Conversation is for students who need a slower pace in the study of language. Students will benefit from more time to study grammar, acquire vocabulary, practice pronunciation and will receive more in-class support on assessments such as projects and memorizations. Students will use Duolingo to guide their program of study. They will also use sites including: Gimkit, Blooket, Wordwall, and Quizlet. This class is for students who want to learn some Spanish and earn a language credit but will not take a second year of language.
notes: Semester Two; Elective

description: The emphasis in Spanish I is on building a vocabulary and learning everyday Spanish. Reading, writing, speaking and listening skills are all stressed in order to build a basic level of proficiency. Students will create a variety of oral and written texts to express their understanding. By the end of this level, students will be able to describe and converse about themselves, their family, their school day and their hobbies.

At the intermediate level, emphasis will be placed on improving the students’ ability to understand spoken Spanish as well as to speak the language more fluidly. Students will create cultural presentations, participate in conversations about current events, and recite songs and poetry. By the end of this level, students should be comfortable carrying on daily conversations regarding topics such as food, shopping, travel and health/medical needs.
prerequisites: Spanish I

description: This course continues the fundamentals of the Spanish language skills covering grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation. Vocabulary units go into depth regarding the ways students spend their time, family dynamics, and daily routines. The course includes conversation, reading and writing exercises and provides an introduction to the arts and cultures of Spain, Latin America and Spanish-speaking peoples.
prerequisites: Spanish II completion w/ 3.0 and teacher recommendation
notes: Listed in the dual enrollment list as CCV Spanish I SPA 1011

description: In Spanish level 4, students now have the skills to conduct a large percent of the class in the target language. Vocabulary units will focus around food, medical needs, and the environment. Students will do hands-on projects in each unit. The English part of class will focus on verb conjugation in the past and future tenses. By the end of four years, students should be proficient meaning they would be able to communicate in most basic situations of daily life.
prerequisites: Spanish III completion w/ 3.0 and teacher recommendation
notes: This course is a concurrent/dual enrollment college class conducted on our campus, led by Ms. McBride. Listed in the dual enrollment list as CCV Spanish II SPA 1012

description: Pathways is a system that facilitates flexible and challenging individual and personal learning plans designed to recognize and nurture unique learning styles, interests, and strengths of individual students, and supports multiple pathways towards achievement and assessment of proficiencies. Individual paths for students can include, but are not limited to: experiential, service, blended, independent, online, skill-based, work-readiness, advanced college-readiness, and traditional learning. You will meet with your advisor and the Coordinator of Student Support in your school to discuss these options.
notes: program; *see the Pathways section of this guide for more information*

description: This course focuses on the fundamental disciplines of woodworking; that is, the proper execution of the basic skills and attention to detail leading to the development of self-confidence. Projects are designed to reinforce previously learned fundamentals. There is a heavy emphasis on hand tools although competency with power tools is also developed. Students choose projects of progressive complexity and utility; including carving of lettering, sculpture and small furniture making.

All freshmen will take this team-taught multidisciplinary course. This supportive course is designed to help support our freshmen as they transition to high school. Teachers will focus on organization, projects, executive functioning, team building, reading, writing, math, and myriad other skills. The team of teachers who run this course have designed it as a “bridge” between middle & high school expectations.
notes: All freshmen will take this course

description: This course will cover the important issues that you will encounter during your high school years; and help to prepare you for life beyond high school. We will investigate life management skills in the areas of personal, family, and community living; wellness, nutrition, and foods; consumer management (budgeting), living environments and job readiness. Students can take this class more than once with teacher permission.

AP Computer Science Principles is an introductory college-level computing course that introduces students to the breadth of the field of computer science. Students learn to design and evaluate solutions and to apply computer science to solve problems through the development of algorithms and programs. They incorporate abstraction into programs and use data to discover new knowledge. Students also explain how computing innovations and computing systems—including the internet—work, explore their potential impacts, and contribute to a computing culture that is collaborative and ethical.
notes: Description titled AP Computer Science Principles

description: This course is designed to equip middle/high school athletes with the knowledge and skills necessary to pursue collegiate sports opportunities successfully. Students will explore key aspects of athletic preparation, including coaching principles, strength and conditioning tailored for their sport, and game film analysis to enhance performance. They will also develop athlete profiles, learn proper sports nutrition, and practice interview techniques to effectively present themselves to recruiters. Additionally, the course emphasizes sportsmanship, leadership, and the mental aspects of competition, ensuring students are well-rounded and prepared for the next level of their athletic journey.

The purpose of a Work-Based Learning is to provide an opportunity for juniors and seniors to gain on the job experience in a specific field of interest. Students connect classroom experiences to community and career experiences to prepare them for the future. We are hoping to offer this option in the future.
notes: program; "We are hoping to offer this option in the future."

description: Students may earn graduation PIs/credit via online courses. Our two current vendors are Vermont Virtual Learning Cooperative (VTVLC) and Brigham Young University (BYU). VTVLC is a partnership of Vermont schools that offer online courses that may not otherwise be available at NMHS or WMHS. The school assumes the cost of these courses. Prior approval from the Coordinator of Student Support is required. The course/grade will be recorded on the student’s transcript.

description: Introduction to College and Careers is a free 13-week course that provides students with the opportunity to explore the college experience within the context of their future career goals. For more information and a schedule of courses at all 12 CCV locations, please visit: www.gotocollegevt.org
notes: program; free 13-week course

description: Habits of Success are earned based on the student’s ability to demonstrate how they achieved them through their individual experience. HOS are approved by the supervisor and school counselor. Students will engage in direct personal service under an approved plan developed by the student and authorized by the school counselor. Service Learning builds character, empathy, commitment and engagement, all key qualities of both Northfield High School and of caring citizens. Students are responsible for keeping a weekly log documenting hours worked. Possibilities include: tutoring other students, helping senior citizens, improving the school or larger community.
notes: program
